records.title: BRCA2 C-terminal clamp restructures RAD51 dimers to bind B-DNA for replication fork stability
records.abstract: Tumor suppressor protein breast cancer susceptibility protein 2 (BRCA2) acts with RAD51 in replication fork protection (FP) and homology-directed DNA-break repair (HDR). Critical for cancer etiology and therapy resistance, the BRCA2 C terminus was thought to stabilize recombinogenic RAD51 after the assembly of ATP-extended RAD51 filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). Here, the detailed crystal structure of the human BRCA2 C-terminal interaction domain (TR2 interface [TR2i]) complexed with ATP-bound RAD51 prior to DNA binding instead reveals TR2i unexpectedly induces a unique ATP-RAD51 dimer conformation that accommodates nucleation onto double-stranded B-DNA unsuited for HDR initiation. Structural, biochemical, and molecular results with interface-guided mutations uncover TR2i’s FP mechanism. Proline-driven secondary structure stabilizes residue triads and spans the RAD51 dimer, engaging pivotal interactions of RAD51 M210 and BRCA2 S3291/P3292, the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation site that toggles between FP during S phase and HDR in G2. TR2i evidently acts as an allosteric clamp, switching RAD51 from ssDNA to double-stranded and B-DNA binding, enforcing FP over HDR, challenging the current BRCA2-RAD51 dogma.

records.abstract: Introduction : Les apparentés au premier degré de patients atteints de cancer colorectal (CCR) ou d’adénome avancé avant l’âge de 65 ans (patients index) présentent un risque accru de CCR, mais les lignes directrices relatives au dépistage familial des apparentés par coloscopie sont peu suivies. Cette étude a pour objectif de décrire, d’un point de vue linguistique et sociologique, l’implication de spécialistes en médecine générale auprès des patients (apparentés à risque élevé de cancer colorectal ou patients index) et leur posture communicationnelle dans le cadre du dépistage familial auprès des différents protagonistes (autres médecins, patients index, apparentés). Méthode : Elle s’appuie sur 29 entretiens semi-directifs avec des spécialistes en médecine générale français de patients index et/ou de leurs apparentés réalisés par téléphone. Le corpus entièrement transcrit des entretiens a fait l’objet d’une analyse linguistique à l’aide d’un outil lexicométrique qui permet de déterminer les objets de discours et d’une analyse sociologique thématique. records.title: A Comprehensive Review on Thyroid Management And Therapeutic Potential of Medicinal Plants
records.abstract: Thyroid diseases are widespread endocrine disorders that affect a significant portion of the global population. The pathology associated with specific types or stages of thyroid disease is complex and intricately linked to various biological functions. While the mortality rate associated with thyroid dysfunction is relatively low, it can lead to metabolic and immunological disorders that result in considerable discomfort for affected individuals. Currently, numerous pharmaceutical options are available for managing thyroid disease; however, issues such as drug toxicity and prolonged treatment durations highlight the urgent need for more effective alternatives. Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent endocrine conditions worldwide, affecting individuals across all age groups and contributing significantly to morbidity and reduced quality of life. Effective thyroid management requires accurate diagnosis, appropriate therapeutic interventions, and long-term monitoring to prevent complications and optimize patient outcomes.

records.title: Water Lily or Camelotte Sign in Pulmonary Hydatid Cyst – An Orphan Disease
records.abstract: A 20 – year – old male without any previous comorbidity presented to pulmonary medicine outpatient department with complaints of dull aching chest pain on right side, dry cough and shortness of breath for the pastone year. He was non vegetarian and had no addictions. On general physical examination his vitals were stableand respiratory system examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right hemithorax. All his routineblood investigations were normal. Chest radiograph revealed homogenous opacity in the right middle andlower zones. Contrast enhanced computed tomography of thorax and abdomen showed a well defined encapsulatedcystic lesion of size 12x10x14cm with internal floating membranes (water lily sign or Camelotte sign) with masseffect on adjacent lung parenchyma causing atelectasis and compression of adjacent vessels (Figure 1). Hydatid serology (IgG) was positive. Patient was treated symptomatically and referred for surgical intervention.

records.title: Caracterización clínica y epidemiológica de la bronquitis aguda en pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años durante 2023
records.abstract: Introducción: La bronquitis aguda es una de las infecciones respiratorias más frecuentes en la población pediátrica y representa una causa importante de consulta y hospitalización en América Latina. Metodología: Se realizó un estudio observacional, descriptivo, transversal y retrospectivo mediante revisión de historias clínicas electrónicas de 83 pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años con diagnóstico de bronquitis aguda atendidos durante enero–diciembre de 2023. Resultados: Predominó el sexo masculino (61,4%) y el grupo de 2 a 4 años (44,6%). La tos fue la manifestación más frecuente (92,8%), seguida de fiebre (62,7%) y sibilancias (51,8%). Las complicaciones más frecuentes fueron la exacerbación del asma (10,8%) y la otitis media aguda (8,4%). Los broncodilatadores inhalados fueron el tratamiento más utilizado (75,9%), seguidos de antipiréticos (72,3%); los antibióticos se emplearon en 13,3%. Conclusiones: La bronquitis aguda presentó predominio masculino, mayor frecuencia en niños de 2 a 4 años y una presentación clínica caracterizada principalmente por tos. Las complicaciones graves fueron poco frecuentes y el uso de antibióticos fue limitado.

affiliations: School of Medicine, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, TX, USA.
records.abstract: Background Positive paediatric cancer treatment outcomes in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs) significantly lag behind those in high-income countries. One reason for this disparity is high treatment abandonment rates in LMICs, defined as a failure to start or complete curative-intent therapy after a cancer diagnosis. We did a systematic review and meta-analysis to describe interventions aimed at reducing treatment abandonment in paediatric patients with cancer in LMICs. Methods In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we completed a comprehensive search of MEDLINE Ovid, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane on Oct 21, 2022, with an updated search on Oct 21, 2025. Studies were included if they met the following criteria: studied an intervention on treatment abandonment; included patients with cancer aged 18 years and younger; were conducted in LMICs as defined by the World Bank income classification; contained quantification of treatment abandonment by patients in a comparison and intervention group; and had a full-text article available. We restricted inclusion to English-language studies. We systematically assessed the quality of the studies and conducted a random-effects meta-analysis of risk ratios. Findings Among the 2263 articles identified across the two searches, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. records.title: 2022 WHO estimates for overall and human papillomavirus test-based cervical cancer screening coverage worldwide: a review and synthetic analysis.
affiliations: Cancer Epidemiology Research Program, Catalan Institute of Oncology, Bellvitge Biomedical Research Institute (IDIBELL), L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Barcelona, Spain; Centro de Investigación Biomédica en Red de Epidemiología y Salud Pública (CIBERESP CB06/02/0073), Madrid, Spain; Programa de Doctorat en Medicina i Recerca Translacional, Universitat de Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain.
records.abstract: Background Regularly updated global estimates are needed to monitor progress in cervical cancer screening, a key pillar of WHO's strategy to eliminate cervical cancer. We aimed to update estimates of cervical cancer screening coverage in 194 WHO member states and eight associated countries and territories for 2022, including the first global assessment of human papillomavirus (HPV) test-based screening adoption and roll-out. Methods In this review and synthetic analysis, we used an established method to estimate standardised cervical cancer screening coverage in 2022. We used programme and population-based coverage data collected up to Jan 31, 2024, selecting the sources considered most representative of each country or territory's screening situation in 2022. Preliminary estimates were reviewed through a WHO country consultation (April-May, 2024; with additional responses received until July 2025). HPV testing coverage was estimated based on HPV test-based screening implementation levels, by country and year. Estimates were applied to 2022 populations and aggregated by region and country-income level. Findings Cervical cancer screening recommendations were identified in 161 (80%) of 202 countries, with 92 (57%) of 161 countries recommending HPV test-based screening. records.title: Perineal Urethrostomy After Urethral Stricture: Step-by-Step Surgical Technique.
affiliations: Serviço de Urologia, Hospital Federal da Lagoa, Rio de Janeiro, RJ, Brasil.
records.abstract: Purpose Urethral stricture is a chronic narrowing of the urethral lumen caused by inflammation and iatrogenic interventions, including previous surgery and prostate cancer treatment (1). Treatment options include urethral dilation, internal urethrotomy, urethroplasty, and perineal urethrostomy. Perineal urethrostomy creates a permanent urethral meatus and is increasingly considered a primary treatment option for complex cases or patients with significant comorbidities (2, 3). It is associated with high patient satisfaction, preserved continence, and favorable voiding outcomes (4). This video presents a systematic, step-by-step description of the surgical technique. Materials and methods A 73-year-old man with complex, recurrent urethral stricture had undergone multiple reconstructive and endoscopic procedures before perineal urethrostomy in February 2026. His medical history was notable for Bowen's disease of the glans penis. Under spinal anesthesia, with the patient in the high lithotomy position, an inverted U-shaped perineal incision was made, and the bulbocavernosus muscle was dissected to expose the bulbar urethra. The perineal skin was sutured to the opened urethra, incorporating the urethral mucosal edge, corpus spongiosum adventitia, and skin edge. The dorsal urethral plate was left intact, preserving longitudinal blood flow within the corpus spongiosum. A Foley catheter was inserted through the proximal urethrotomy into the bladder. records.abstract: PURPOSE: This study presents a structured narrative review of lower urinary tract (LUT) complications following prostate cancer (PCa) radiotherapy and proposes an organ-based clinical framework for their evaluation and management. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, including studies published between January 2000 and December 2025 and supplemented by seminal studies in radiation biology and reconstructive urology. Search terms included prostate cancer, radiotherapy, radiation cystitis, bladder dysfunction, urethral stricture, bladder neck contracture, urinary incontinence, urinary fistulae, ureteral stricture, and post-radiotherapy outlet surgery. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively and organized into organ-specific domains. RESULTS: Radiation-induced LUT complications include radiation cystitis, detrusor overactivity and impaired compliance associated with bladder fibrosis, urethral and bladder neck strictures, sphincteric insufficiency with urinary incontinence, urinary fistulae, and ureteral strictures. These conditions frequently coexist because of the multifocal and progressive nature of radiation injury. Management is challenging because tissue hypovascularity, fibrosis, and impaired healing increase the risks of recurrence, infection, erosion, and fistula formation. records.title: Multiphoton Imaging of the Tibial Bone Marrow for In Vivo Spatial-Temporal Analysis of Myeloma Microenvironment and Treatment.
affiliations: Department of Pathology, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Bronx, NY, USA. david.fooksman@einsteinmed.edu.
records.abstract: The bone marrow is a critical niche for multiple myeloma initiation, growth, and pathology. The biological and technical complexities of the bone marrow microenvironment make it challenging to study tumor physiology in situ. We have developed a thinned-bone surgical preparation for imaging the mouse tibial bone marrow. Using this approach, we have studied the spatial organization and temporal dynamics of myeloma cells, their interactions with the immune microenvironment, and the effects of acute drug treatments. In this chapter, we detail a protocol describing this procedure and present two use cases for intravital imaging to study dynamics tumors. In one study, we describe the use of photoactivation to capture live immune cells that are present within myeloma foci within the bone marrow for downstream analysis by flow cytometry or by other methods. In the second use case, we used imaging to capture effects of drug treatment in real-time in situ in the bone marrow to understand mechanisms of action and side effects.

records.title: Measurable Residual Disease.
affiliations: Department of Hematopathology, ACTREC, Tata Memorial Center, HBNI University, Room 18, CCE Building, ACTREC, Sector 22, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai, 410210, India. docprt@gmail.com.
records.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) serves as a critical biomarker of prognosis, treatment efficacy, and clinical outcome. It captures the presence of residual tumor cells below the detection threshold of conventional microscopy. Multiparametric flow cytometry (MFC) offers a rapid, cost-efficient, and widely applicable platform for MRD detection through leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIPs) and deviation-from-normal (DfN) antigen maturation patterns. This technique underpins a wide range of clinical applications, including risk stratification, therapeutic decision-making, and post-transplant surveillance. This chapter outlines essential technical parameters for achieving high-sensitivity MRD detection across hematologic malignancies such as B-ALL, T-ALL, AML, MM, and CLL. Key topics covered include material required, reagent preparation, antibody panel design, sample processing and acquisition, gating strategies, and illustrative examples. Special emphasis is given to adaptations necessary for MRD monitoring following CD19-targeted therapies in B-ALL. By integrating rigorous methodology with evolving innovations, MFC continues to advance as a precise and expedient tool for MRD assessment, contributing significantly to personalized treatment strategies.

Markers such as CD38, CD27, and CD24 are helpful to identify plasmablasts and immature B cells. CD21 points to mature B cells, CD10 is on immature B cells, CD138 marks plasma cells, and CD5 is high in regulatory B cells. Memory B cells have less CD23 than naïve B cells. B cells are multifaceted. They present antigens (APCs), secrete antibodies, and keep the immune system in check. Knowing which B cells are present in a certain disease setting helps clinicians understand how far a disease has progressed and how active it is. With flow cytometry as a tool, we can spot B-cell malignancies like chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), follicular lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, and multiple myeloma. records.abstract: We are conducting a scoping review focusing on the topic of "family accommodation", defined as “actions that family members engage in, or deliberately do not engage in, to help alleviate or avoid a child’s distress” in parents of children, adolescents and young adults (CAYA) with a cancer diagnosis. The premise underpinning this review is the notion that parental accommodation may negatively impact child’s health, health-related behaviours, and mental health. The scoping review aims to explore: 1) How does parental accommodation impact the health, health-related behaviours, and mental health of CAYA with a cancer diagnosis; 2) how does parental accommodation impact the emotional and psychological well-being of parents in families with CAYA with a cancer diagnosis; and 3) how is family accommodation in the context of cancer being measured.

Such pathological processes contribute to both immediate clinical instability and long-term complications such as fibrosis, aberrant bone formation, neuroinflammation, and chronic disability. records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: AIMS: Tumour budding (TB) has been recognized as an additional prognostic factor in the TNM (2017) and WHO (2019) classification systems. However, its prognostic impact in stages II and III colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inconsistently defined. This study aims to systematically evaluate the prognostic value of high-grade TB in stage II-III CRC. METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase and Cochrane Library was conducted to identify studies reporting the association between high-grade TB and survival outcomes in stage II-III CRC. A total of 43 studies involving 17,831 patients were included. Subgroup analysis stratified by TNM stage revealed that high-grade TB consistently predicted adverse outcomes in both stage II and stage III disease. records.abstract: The glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich layer formed by glycoproteins, glycolipids, proteoglycans, and glycosaminoglycans at the outer cell surface. In cancer, this layer is not a passive coating. Its thickness, composition, charge, and nanoscale organization are altered by oncogenic signaling, dysregulated glycosyltransferases, protease-mediated shedding, and reciprocal interactions with stromal and immune cells. These changes affect how tumor cells sense force, bind the extracellular matrix, cluster receptors, evade immune surveillance, survive in circulation, and arrest at distant vascular beds. Studies in the past decade have linked a bulky glycocalyx to integrin activation and growth factor signaling, identified hyaluronan-CD44 and selectin-dependent steps in metastatic dissemination, and placed the sialoglycan-Siglec axis among the immune suppressive circuits operating in the tumor microenvironment. Meanwhile, pathology, imaging, glycoproteomics, and liquid-biopsy studies have started to define glycocalyx-derived biomarkers with diagnostic and prognostic value, especially in hepatocellular carcinoma, pancreatic cancer, breast cancer, and hematologic malignancies. This review summarizes the structure of the cancer glycocalyx, the molecular programs that remodel it, and the consequences of these changes for tumor progression. records.abstract: Esophageal candidiasis is commonly associated with HIV infection but also occurs in patients without HIV. This systematic review aimed to summarize risk factors for esophageal candidiasis in non-HIV patients. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect were searched for studies evaluating risk factors in non-HIV populations or reporting non-HIV subgroups separately, and the findings were synthesized qualitatively. Four studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising retrospective case–control and prospective observational studies in endoscopy-based settings. Reported prevalence among non-HIV patients ranged from 0.34% to 8.99%, depending on the population and case ascertainment. Dysphagia and odynophagia predicted esophageal candidiasis in one prospective study, whereas a retrospective study found no correlation between symptoms and endoscopic severity. records.title: Triage models for surgical decision-making in patients with shoulder pain: an integrative review.
affiliations: St. Joseph's Hospital
St Joseph's Health Care
Western University
Lawson Research Institute
records.abstract: Shoulder pain is a major cause of work absenteeism, affecting 1 in 3 adults. Although nonsurgical treatments like physical therapy are recommended as the first line of management, 40% of patients are referred for surgery before exploring these options. This review aimed to identify existing triage models used for shoulder pain referrals for surgery, guidelines for shoulder pain management that include criteria for surgical referral, and indications for surgery. An integrative review approach was used to comprehensively search major databases (Medline, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL Plus) and gray literature. Articles on triage models, referral processes, or surgery candidacy for shoulder pain were included. The searches retrieved 4510 articles, with 480 selected for full review and 71 articles included in this synthesis. Thirty-seven articles described various triage models and clinical decision-making processes for managing shoulder pain, including determining when to refer for surgical consultation and the indications for surgery. Seventeen articles compared surgical and nonsurgical treatments to identify surgical indicators, 10 articles examined factors affecting decision-making, and 7 articles explored predictor models for surgical outcomes. The findings underscore the need for a multifactorial decision-making process that acknowledges the complexity of pain within a biopsychosocial framework and incorporates patients' personal preferences into the triage decision-making process.

Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. Next, I tested whether testosterone and estrogen affected how well cannabinoids worked as pain relievers. I found that testosterone reduced the drug’s efficacy in females, while estrogens reduced its efficacy in males. records.title: Thiolutin alleviates acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) in a mouse model of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
affiliations: Anhui Medical University

Beijing Institute of Microbiology and Epidemiology
records.abstract: Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) is a major, life-threatening complication in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and the development of novel molecular-targeted therapies for aGVHD is urgently needed. Thiolutin (THL), a disulfide-containing antibiotic, inhibits the activity of the BRCC3-containing isopeptidase complex and thereby suppresses NLR pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation. Here, we investigated the effect of THL on aGVHD in a mouse model of allo-HSCT. We found that THL significantly improved survival in aGVHD recipients, reduced weight loss and clinical scores, and attenuated pathological changes in aGVHD target organs, including the liver, small intestine, and colon. Furthermore, THL diminished donor T-cell activation and infiltration into target organs and promoted the expansion of regulatory T cells. THL also inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation and reduced the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interferon γ (IFN-γ), interleukin (IL)-2, IL-17A, and IL-1β. This study reveals a previously unrecognized role of THL in regulating aGVHD and highlights its potential as an anti-inflammatory therapeutic agent for clinical development in patients undergoing allo-HSCT.

records.abstract: Neural crest cells (NCCs) are a transient, highly migratory embryonic stem cell population unique to vertebrates. During development, they give rise to diverse tissues, including craniofacial cartilage, peripheral neurons, glia, melanocytes, and components of the cardiac outflow tract. As NCCs migrate through complex environments, precise spatial and temporal regulation of gene expression is needed to coordinate migration and developmental fate. Defects in NCC development and migration can result in a broad class of disorders known as neurocristopathies (NCPs), including craniofacial abnormalities, Hirschsprung’s disease, and neuroblastoma. Despite the importance of NCC migration during development, many of the molecular mechanisms regulating this process are still not fully understood. One mechanism that enables spatial regulation of gene expression is RNA localization, the transport of messenger RNAs (mRNAs) to specific subcellular regions. Previous work, including studies from our lab, demonstrated that in other migratory cell types, specific mRNAs localize to cellular protrusions and contribute to efficient migration. Interestingly, in these systems, disruption of mRNA localization alone is enough to reduce migratory efficiency, suggesting that RNA localization itself plays an important role in regulating migration. affiliations: Utah State University
records.abstract: Adolescence is a period of rapid growth and development during which good nutrition is especially important for long-term health. However, many adolescents in the United States consume large amounts of ultra-processed foods, including packaged snacks, sugary drinks, and fast food. This dissertation used nationally representative data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017–2020 to examine micronutrient intake, ultra-processed food consumption, food-related behaviors, and metabolic health among U.S. adolescents. The first part of the study examined usual nutrient intake and micronutrient adequacy. Overall micronutrient adequacy was high at 96%. However, important dietary concerns remained. Many adolescents had low intakes of calcium and magnesium and consumed high amounts of saturated fat, added sugars, and sodium. Adolescents who used dietary supplements had higher intakes of several vitamins and minerals, but supplement use did not eliminate all nutrient shortfalls. Ultra-processed foods contributed about two-thirds of total daily energy intake, with differences observed across demographic groups. The second part examined whether food-related behaviors were associated with ultra-processed food consumption and micronutrient adequacy. More frequent fast-food consumption was associated with a higher estimated share of energy from ultra-processed foods, although this relationship was not statistically conclusive. records.title: [Advances in precision management of aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia in breast cancer].
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
records.abstract: Endocrine therapy is a core strategy throughout the management of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, substantially reducing the risks of recurrence and death. However, treatment-related adverse events, particularly aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia (AIA), have become a major barrier to treatment adherence. Current evidence suggests that AIA cannot be explained solely by estrogen deprivation. T-cell leukemia/lymphoma 1A (TCL1A) genetic variants, interleukin-17/nuclear factor-κB-related inflammatory pathways, and an imbalance between T helper 17 and regulatory T cells may jointly contribute to its development, suggesting that AIA may represent a modifiable pathological process. Accordingly, its management should shift from symptom-oriented palliation toward a precise supportive-care model integrating risk stratification, early intervention, and long-term adherence maintenance. From a translational medicine perspective, this review synthesizes evidence on the pathogenesis of AIA, intervention trials, and the latest guidelines, and proposes a three-stage AIA management framework adapted to Chinese clinical practice (baseline assessment and prevention-stratified intervention-digital closed-loop follow-up). The framework emphasizes the importance of alleviating adverse events to maintain treatment adherence and improve long-term outcomes but requires prospective clinical validation.

records.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNA molecules that are mainly generated from precursor mRNAs through back-splicing. In aquatic animals, recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis have greatly expanded the catalog of circRNAs and uncovered their regulatory roles in growth, gonadal development, tissue regeneration, immune defense, and environmental stress responses. This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. We further summarize the current evidence associating circRNAs with candidate biomarker potential for economically important traits, infectious disease monitoring, and ecotoxicological assessment. Importantly, we highlight the major bottlenecks that currently limit progress in this field, including incomplete genome annotation, algorithm-dependent identification bias, and the lack of robust in vivo functional validation. Research shows that children with cancer are at risk for psychopathology, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety and depression. Thus, the aim of the proposed research is to delineate factors that may predict psychopathology among children with cancer. In line with central theories of emotional disorders (Mathews & MacLeod, 2005), we focus on cognitive biases involving processing threat-related information, and their relation to psychopathology. The children in the active phase of the treatment and those in remission will perform several cognitive tasks, assessing attention bias, working memory bias, and memory bias. records.title: The MAGOH/hnRNPH1 axis promotes alternative splicing-derived soluble PD-L1 generation and attenuates PD-L1 blockade efficacy in gastric cancer
records.abstract: Abstract Despite the clinical success of PD-1 blockade, the therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1 blockade in gastric cancer (GC) remains limited. Soluble PD-L1 (sPD-L1) has been proposed to function as a decoy that sequesters anti-PD-L1 antibodies, potentially contributing to therapeutic resistance. Our previous study identified an exon 5/6-skipping PD-L1 splice variant, designated PD-L1-v1, as an important source of sPD-L1 in GC. We also found that MAGOH is highly expressed in GC and participates in alternative splicing regulation. Here, we demonstrate that PD-L1-v1 acts as a soluble decoy that limits PD-L1 blocker binding to membrane-bound PD-L1 on tumor cells, thereby impairing the antitumor efficacy of PD-L1 blockade. Mechanistically, MAGOH upregulates hnRNPH1 expression, primarily by enhancing its mRNA stability, and promotes hnRNPH1-dependent exon5/6 skipping of PD-L1 pre-mRNA, thereby facilitating PD-L1-v1 and sPD-L1 generation. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism of resistance to PD-L1 blockade and highlight the MAGOH/hnRNPH1 axis as a potential strategy for improving immunotherapy efficacy in GC.

records.abstract: Abstract Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outlines current computational and experimental techniques to identify, prioritise, and functionally validate non-coding variants in PDAC. We also emphasise new AI-based methods involving radiogenomics, AI imaging analysis and data integration, which provides novel potential to link genomic variation with phenotypic and imaging characteristics. records.title: [Emphasis on the standardization of initial treatment for ovarian cancer].
affiliations: Qilu Hospital of Shandong University
records.abstract: Based on the current technical development status among various regions and medical institutions in China, this article proposes corresponding clinical decision-making pathways to standardize and homogenize the initial treatment of ovarian cancer and optimize patient prognosis. All patients require comprehensive and thorough evaluation by the gynecologic oncology multidisciplinary team. Comprehensive staging surgery is indicated for early-stage ovarian cancer. For advanced cases, primary debulking surgery or interval debulking surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is adopted based on clinical indications, with great emphasis on multidisciplinary expertise and surgical quality to elevate the implementation rate and complete resection rate of the initial debulking surgery. Standard first-line chemotherapy with adequate dosage and full cycles is strongly recommended. For advanced patients who have achieved remission after chemotherapy, genetic testing-guided maintenance therapy is preferred. Regular post-treatment follow-up is essential for early identification of tumor recurrence.

records.title: Echidna: a Bayesian framework for integrative inference of copy number alterations impacting phenotypic plasticity
affiliations: Columbia University
Columbia University Irving Medical Center
University of California, Los Angeles
Stanford University
records.abstract: The ability of cells to adapt their behavior in response to genetic or environmental changes is a fundamental biological process that drives cellular diversity in both normal and pathological contexts, including in tumor evolution. Copy number alterations (CNAs), which can include large-scale changes in genomic ploidy, play a key role in creating adaptive advantages in evolving cell populations. However, tracing these populations across experiments and disentangling the role of CNAs from other sources of transcriptional variability remains challenging and expensive. Here we present Echidna, a Bayesian hierarchical model that integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk whole-genome sequencing data to enable robust integrative inference of CNAs, jointly across samples and treatment time points, to better understand the impact of genomic events on cellular phenotype. Applying Echidna to patient tumor specimens, we demonstrate its superior performance in clonal reconstruction and derive insights into therapy resistance mechanisms. Echidna integrates genomic and transcriptomics data to reveal how copy number alterations shape tumor evolution and therapy resistance.

records.title: Rank-One Convexification for Quadratic Optimization Problems with Switching Constraints
affiliations: University of Southern California
Universidad de Los Andes
National University of Singapore
records.abstract: We investigate convexification for convex quadratic optimization with switching constraints. Such problems can be cast as mixed-integer quadratic optimization problems, where binary variables are used to encode whether a linear inequality is active or not. First, we derive the convex hull for the epigraph of a quadratic function defined by a rank-one matrix and switching penalties. Using this rank-one convexification, we develop copositive and semidefinite relaxations for general convex quadratic functions. Leveraging these findings, we construct convex formulations to the support vector machine problem with 0–1 loss. The resulting methods scale well with the number of data points, provided that the number of features is small. In terms of statistical performance, the proposed methods outperform standard support vector machine problems with hinge loss in data sets corrupted by outliers. Funding: A. Gómez and S. Choi were supported by the Air Force Office of Scientific Research [Grants FA9550-24-1-0086 and FA9550-22-1-0369] and the National Science Foundation [Grants 2152777 and 2112533]. S. Han was supported by the NUS (Suzhou) Research Institute [Grant SZ2025-03] and the Academic Research Fund Tier 1 from the Ministry of Education, Singapore [Grant FY2024]. affiliations: West Virginia University
records.abstract: Cell Communication Network factor 4 (CCN4/WISP1) is a matricellular protein secreted by cancer cells that is upregulated in essentially all invasive breast cancers and promotes immunosuppression in melanoma. Limited anti-tumor immunity associates with poor patient outcomes in breast cancer, and elevated CCN4 correlates with dampened anti-tumor immunity in primary breast cancer tumors. To test for a direct causal link, we knocked out CCN4 in the Py230 and Py8119 syngeneic mouse breast cancer models. CCN4 knockout dramatically prolonged tumor-free survival in immunocompetent but not immunodeficient mice, establishing that CCN4's tumor-promoting effects are immune-dependent. In size-matched tumors, CCN4 knockout increases CD45+ infiltration and shifts the myeloid compartment from polymorphonuclear- to monocytic-myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), changes accompanied by a significant reduction in splenomegaly consistent with a systemic as well as local effect. Analysis of TCGA breast cancer data further reveals that genetic alterations converging on beta-catenin pathway activation, including CCN4 copy number amplification at a frequency comparable to ERBB2, are present in a substantial fraction of invasive breast cancers. records.title: Corilagin increases the sensitivity of neuroblastoma to cisplatin by regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
affiliations: Jiangsu Province Hospital
Xuzhou Medical College
Model Animal Research Center
records.abstract: Drug resistance remains the leading cause of cisplatin treatment failure in neuroblastoma (NB). This study aimed to investigate the potential of corilagin as an adjuvant therapy for overcoming cisplatin resistance in NB. In vitro functional assays—including cell viability (CCK-8), colony formation, transwell migration, and invasion assays—were conducted to evaluate the effects of corilagin in combination with cisplatin on human NB cell lines (SH-SY5Y and SK-N-BE(2)) and a cisplatin-resistant subline (SH-SY5Y/R). In vivo tumorigenesis experiments were performed to assess the suppressive effects of the corilagin-cisplatin combination on tumor growth initiated by SH-SY5Y and SH-SY5Y/R cells in mouse models. RNA sequencing was utilized to identify molecular mechanisms associated with cisplatin resistance and the therapeutic action of corilagin, followed by functional validation using 740Y-P, a specific agonist of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Our results showed that the combination of corilagin and cisplatin significantly inhibited proliferation, migration, invasion, and autophagic activity in SH-SY5Y/R cells, while robustly inducing apoptosis. Importantly, the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway was found to be hyperactivated during the development of cisplatin resistance, whereas corilagin effectively suppressed this activation. These findings indicate that corilagin enhances cisplatin sensitivity in NB cells through modulation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.

records.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies have transformed the capacity to quantify gene expression from human tissues, simultaneously capturing both the cell functional state and spatial organization at cellular and subcellular resolution. The CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager (SMI) is one of the leading platforms at single-cell spatial multi-modal omics profiling, capable of measuring thousands of RNA or protein targets at single-cell and subcellular resolution across whole slide sections. Exported data include field-of-view (FOV) image tiles, subcellular transcript coordinates, and cell segmentation polygons, outputs that are rich in spatial information but not directly compatible with widely used digital pathology tools. Here we present CosMxScope, a lightweight open-source Python framework designed for data exported from the CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager through the AtoMx platform, bridging CosMx spatial outputs with histopathology visualization environments. records.title: Laboratory Models of Hepatitis B and D Viruses: Search for Cell Permissiveness and Restriction Factors
affiliations: Engelhardt Institute of Molecular Biology
Russian Academy of Sciences
Sechenov University
records.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is an oncogenic human pathogen that accounts for 250 mln cases of chronic hepatitis worldwide. Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) is its satellite that substantially aggravates liver disease. The development of new antivirals and the investigation of viral pathogenesis are limited by the absence of effective cellular and animal models. Current cell models are based on human primary hepatocytes, liver progenitor HepaRG cells, iPS-derived hepatocyte-like cells or various hepatoma cells overexpressing the putative NTCP receptor. However, in most of these models, a majority of cells are non-permissive. In this review, we briefly assess these models, summarize the approaches to the increasing infection rates, and discuss the data on proviral and antiviral (restriction) host factors. The data discussed suggest that rates of HBV and HDV infections are limited by hepatocyte polarization and insufficient expression of the NTCP receptor, as well as the existence of additional co-receptors and restriction factors that can act mostly on the virus entry stage.

records.abstract: Abstract Melanoma is an aggressive form of skin cancer. Survival rates are excellent if it is detected early but fall markedly if it metastasises. A key step in early tumour progression is the formation of cell clusters, which can promote metastasis. However, the mechanisms driving cell clustering, and the role of phenotypic heterogeneity in the dynamics of these clusters, remain poorly understood. In this work, we propose a system of ordinary differential equations that models cluster formation dynamics within a coagulation–fragmentation–proliferation framework. Using Bayesian inference, we fit this model to in vitro time-lapse microscopy data from both monoculture and co-culture experiments involving two melanoma phenotypes—proliferative and invasive—to uncover the predominant mechanisms driving cluster formation and how these differ between phenotypes. Additionally, we provide preliminary insights into how clustering behaviour in co-cultures contrasts with that observed in monocultures. The model quantifies phenotypic differences in clustering dynamics: invasive cells in monoculture exhibit nearly threefold higher coagulation rates than proliferative cells, whereas proliferative cells display slightly higher proliferation rates. These differences align with known gene expression profiles. records.title: TIPE2 suppresses adipogenesis via METTL14-mediated m6A methylation and represents a potential therapeutic target for obesity
affiliations: Central Hospital of Zibo
Saint Louis University
University of the Basque Country
Qilu Medical University
records.abstract: Abstract Despite conserved mechanisms maintaining energy homeostasis, the global obesity epidemic continues to rise. Tumor necrosis factor-α-induced protein 8-like 2 (TIPE2) is an anti-inflammatory regulator essential for immune homeostasis, yet its role in adipogenesis remains unclear. Here, we show that TIPE2 expression in human adipose tissue is inversely correlated with body mass index (BMI) and metabolic dysfunction. In mice, Tipe2 deficiency exacerbates diet-induced obesity, hyperglycaemia, and insulin resistance, whereas systemic AAV-mediated TIPE2 overexpression alleviates these phenotypes. In vitro, TIPE2 suppresses adipogenic differentiation in primary preadipocytes. Mechanistically, TIPE2 regulates N6-methyladenosine (m6A) via m6A methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14). Loss of TIPE2 reduces m6A levels and METTL14 expression, whereas METTL14 restoration reverses the pro-adipogenic effects. Furthermore, TIPE2 modulates adipogenesis through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) signaling. Together, these findings identify TIPE2 as a suppressor of adipogenesis via coordinated regulation of METTL14-dependent m6A modification and PPAR-γ signaling.

records.title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
affiliations: Salk Institute for Biological Studies
University of California San Diego
Integrated DNA Technologies (United States)
records.abstract: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR–Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression. Superb-seq integrates CRISPR–Cas9, T7 in situ transcription and scRNA-seq to capture genome edits and gene expression in single cells.

records.title: 4D mitochondrial network assumes distinct and predictive phenotypes through human lung and intestinal epithelial development
affiliations: University of San Diego
University of California San Diego
records.abstract: Abstract Mitochondria form dynamic three-dimensional networks that exhibit a wide range of morphology and motility depending on cell state, cell type, and cell fate. Isolated phenotypes have been described for individual cell states, but how mitochondrial morphology and motility change across the full course of human tissue development has so far been unclear. Human stem cell-derived branching lung and intestinal organoids mimic developing human organs and make these systems accessible. Here we show, by imaging at key developmental time points from human stem cell through mature organoid tissue with lattice light-sheet microscopy, that mitochondrial networks adopt morphology and motility signatures that vary with developmental stage, that mitochondrial and cellular features can be used to predict developmental stage, and that two-dimensional measurements obscure features resolved only in three dimensions over time, yielding an integrated map of mitochondrial phenotypes across human tissue development.

records.title: InferPloidy enables CNV guided tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery from single cell RNA sequencing
affiliations: Dankook University
CHA University Bundang Medical Center
California State University, Long Beach
Seoul National University
records.abstract: Abstract Identifying malignant cells in single-cell gene expression data is essential for understanding tumor heterogeneity, but existing computational methods can be slow and perform inconsistently across datasets. Here, we present InferPloidy, a framework that combines graph-based cell grouping with iterative probabilistic modeling to distinguish cells with normal and altered chromosome copy numbers using profiles generated by InferCNV. Across breast, lung, pancreatic, and colorectal cancer datasets, the evaluated workflow reduces computation time by up to two orders of magnitude compared with existing tools and improves agreement with published cell annotations. This classification supports the identification of established therapeutic targets and candidate cell surface markers associated with tumor subtypes. The low proportion of unclassified cells helps preserve information for downstream analyses of gene expression differences and tumor population characteristics. These findings support InferPloidy as an efficient framework for tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery within the evaluated workflow. Its performance with inputs from other copy number inference methods requires further validation.

records.title: SVP Maps Spatially Variable Functional Programs and Their Coupling in Spatial Transcriptomics
affiliations: Southern Medical University
Shenzhen Bay Laboratory
Zhejiang University
Jiangsu Cancer Hospital
records.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has made tissue architecture measurable at molecular resolution, yet most computational methods still identify spatially variable genes and infer biology only indirectly. We present SVP, a framework that directly maps spatially variable cell states, pathways and regulatory programs from spatial transcriptomic data. SVP combines location-level functional activity inference with global and local spatial autocorrelation and extends these analyses to bivariate spatial coupling across heterogeneous features. Across simulations and real datasets, SVP recovered cell-state-associated activity patterns at individual captured locations, detected spatially variable features with calibrated statistics, and scaled efficiently to large datasets. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, SVP identified a spatially co-organized hypoxic and extracellular-matrix-remodeling niche that co-localized with regions of low immune activity. It further captured functional maturation in the developing human heart and plaque-associated glial programs in Alzheimer's disease models. SVP enables direct analysis of functional spatial organization, moving beyond gene-centric descriptions of tissue structure.

records.title: Neuronal cell line expressing full-length mutant huntingtin displays alteration of proteasome activity
affiliations: Lomonosov Moscow State University
Russian Academy of Sciences
Institute of Bioorganic Chemistry
records.abstract: Polyglutamine diseases are incurable genetic neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the accumulation of extended polyglutamine fragments-containing mutant proteins, which are prone to the formation of poorly soluble aggregates. The adequate cellular model is crucial in uncovering the pathological mechanisms responsible for neurotoxicity in Huntington’s disease (HD), screening for therapeutic molecules and elucidation of the molecular mechanisms impacted by particular compound. In the present study, genetic constructs based on the Sleeping Beauty system were created for the stable inducible expression of full-length normal and mutant huntingtin (HTT) in eukaryotic cells. These constructs were then employed to develop model neuronal cells using Neuro-2a cell line. The expression of HTT as well as the accumulation of HTT-immunopositive intracellular aggregates (most characteristic features of HD) was demonstrated, and these aggregates showed colocalization with the proteasome. The activation of the proteasome, as well as changes in the expression of proteasome regulators, components of the autophagy system, and the neuronal proteases cathepsins B and D, reflect the versatility of cellular responses to the mutant pathological forms of HTT.

affiliations: The First People's Hospital of Shunde
Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital

records.abstract: Background The impact of clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), a novel cardiovascular risk factor, remains unclear in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), where cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the main cause of mortality. Methods We analysed data from 140,086 UK Biobank participants with MASLD. CHIP was identified via whole-exome sequencing. Incident CVD, including coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, and heart failure (HF), was the primary outcome. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association between CHIP and CVD risk. Results During a median 13.5-year follow-up, 15.7% of participants developed CVD. CHIP was associated with a higher risk of CVD (HR: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09–1.23), with higher risks of stroke (HR: 1.22, 95% CI: 1.07–1.38) and HF (HR: 1.34, 95% CI: 1.21–1.49). Mutations in ASXL1, SRSF2, JAK2 , and SF3B1 were associated with a particularly high CVD risk. Additionally, a higher clonal haematopoiesis risk score (CHRS) was associated with incident CVD, CHD, stroke, and HF. In the three-category analysis, the P value for trend was significant for all outcomes, but the association was confined to large CHIP for CVD and CHD, whereas both CHIP categories showed elevated estimates for stroke and HF. Conclusions CHIP is independently associated with incident CVD in patients with MASLD. These findings support prospective evaluation of CHIP-informed cardiovascular risk stratification in this population.

records.abstract: Abstract The technologies for implant fabrication are improving every year. Currently, there is a significant demand for implants that not only exhibit high biocompatibility but also possess antibacterial, antiresorptive, and antitumor properties. The data obtained suggests the successful formation of a coating based on the titanium alloy and demonstrates the bioactive properties of the surface layers.

records.abstract: Background: Endometrial cancer remains a therapeutic challenge, particularly in advanced and recurrent cases. Methods: Cell viability was assessed using the CCK-8 assay, while Ki67 expression, apoptosis, cell cycle distribution, mitochondrial membrane potential, and intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were evaluated using immunofluorescence staining and flow cytometry-based assays. Results: All three CDDO derivatives reduced the viability-associated metabolic activity of Ishikawa cells and were associated with changes in Ki67 positivity, apoptosis, and cell cycle distribution. In addition, treatment with the compounds was associated with reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and decreased intracellular ROS-associated fluorescence. Conclusion: These findings demonstrate that treatment with RTA 404, RTA dh404, and RTA 408 is associated with reduced viability-associated metabolic activity, increased Annexin V positivity, altered cell-cycle distributions, and mitochondrial depolarization in Ishikawa endometrial cancer cells. Further mechanistic studies are required to determine the molecular pathways underlying these cellular responses.

records.abstract: Objectives: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among Kenyan women aged 15–44. Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) in women with HIV (WHIV) is more likely to progress in severity compared with women without HIV. This study assesses the results of cryotherapy or LEEP for CIN among WHIV compared with women without HIV in Western Kenya. Methods: Eighty-six WHIV (39 cryotherapy, 47 LEEP) and 89 women without HIV (46 cryotherapy, 43 LEEP) who had follow-up within 24 months were included in this analysis. Women ineligible for cryotherapy underwent colposcopy/biopsy, and those with confirmed CIN 2/3 underwent LEEP. Women were followed every 6 months with VIA, Pap smear or colposcopy/biopsy. χ 2 and Fisher exact tests were used to compare the proportions. Results: There was a significant difference in overall treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV (15.12% vs 5.62% p =.039). There was a significant difference in treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV who underwent cryotherapy (18% vs 2.1%, p =.021). Among patients who underwent LEEP, no difference was observed in the treatment failure rates between WHIV and women without HIV (12.8% vs 9.3%, p =.742). Conclusions: In our experience, LEEP is a more effective treatment than cryotherapy for WHIV compared with women without HIV for CIN in Western Kenya.

records.title: Faith- and community-led service posts narrow HIV case finding, treatment and viral suppression gaps among men in Zambia, 2018–2022
affiliations: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
Imperial College London
records.abstract: HIV testing and treatment coverage among men in Zambia remains suboptimal due to barriers that limit their engagement in care. To address these gaps, Circle of Hope, a local faith-based organization, established Community Posts that provided HIV testing, antiretroviral therapy, and viral load monitoring through multidisciplinary teams. We analyzed routine program data to assess HIV case finding, treatment initiation, retention, and viral load suppression among men attending Community Posts during two implementation periods: April 2018–March 2020 and April 2020–March 2022. Between 2018 and 2022, the number of Community Posts expanded from 9 to 38 nationwide. The proportion of men tested declined from 49.5% to 41.4%, while the proportion diagnosed (38.5% to 42.0%) and initiated on treatment (38.9% to 43.3%) increased significantly (p < 0.001). Men receiving treatment increased from 3,320 to 13,580. Retention and viral load suppression remained consistently high, increasing from 94.1% to 97.2% and 95.2% to 96.1%, respectively. Over 6,000 men were diagnosed through index testing, with high positivity ranging from 54.4%–61.1%. Community Posts improved HIV case finding, treatment initiation and viral suppression, even during the COVID-19 pandemic, supporting the potential of this scalable, faith- and community-led model to help close persistent HIV service gaps among men.

records.abstract: Introduction: Ovarian cancer is characterized by high recurrence rates and complex metabolic reprogramming. A two-dimensional radiomic approach was adopted using the axial CT slice showing the largest tumor area. Tumor regions were manually segmented, and handcrafted radiomic features were extracted using a custom pipeline developed in Python. Statistical comparisons between groups were performed using the Mann–Whitney U test with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Tumors with higher metabolic activity tended to exhibit larger morphologic dimensions and subtle texture alterations.

affiliations: National Chung Cheng University

records.abstract: Abstract Gene delivery using retroviral replicating vectors (RRVs) is highly efficient, with nearly full transduction occurring throughout tumors in small-animal glioma models. However, vector spread is still restricted by the dosage that can be delivered by a single injection of viral vector supernatant, particularly in the large and diffusely infiltrating tumors that are characteristic of human high-grade gliomas. This study attempted to further improve the efficacy of this approach by engineering adult human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) to function as the carrier and producer cells for RRVs. We investigated the capability of RRV-producing hASCs (hASC-RRVs) to yield RRVs and deliver the vector to gliomas. The results show that RRVs released from hASC-RRVs can efficiently infect glioma cells, achieving tumor-selective and persistent gene delivery to gliomas. We have also confirmed the tumor-tropic migratory ability of hASC-RRVs, which greatly improved the efficiency of RRV delivery in vivo . In addition, the therapeutic effect of RRVs delivered by hASCs was increased markedly. In an orthotopic mouse model of human glioma, after a single injection of hASC-RRVs, hASC-RRV-mediated prodrug activator gene therapy resulted in chronic suppression of tumor growth and prolonged survival of the animals. Thus, using hASCs as the carrier and producer for RRVs may represent a promising strategy for glioma gene therapy.

records.abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is the most prevalent malignancy among women worldwide. In summary, E6/E7 promotes cell cycle progression and tumor initiating capacity via activation of the TGFB2–TGF-β–ID1 axis, providing mechanistic insight into HPV associated breast malignant transformation.

affiliations: Xinyang Agriculture and Forestry University
records.abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the acute and subchronic toxicity of sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) on gill tissue of bighead carp ( Hypophthalmichthys nobilis ). Correlation analyses confirmed oxidative stress as the primary mechanism. These findings demonstrate that SDBS causes substantial gill damage via oxidative pathways, posing ecological risks to local freshwater ecosystems.

affiliations: Yunnan Normal University
records.abstract: Abstract Background Small cancer cohorts are routinely used to test driver–phenotype associations, and negative results from them enter the literature as evidence that no association exists. Methods We derived a closed-form detection frontier, d min (n,p) — the smallest standardised effect detectable at 80% power, two-sided α = 0.05, in a two-group comparison of total size n with alteration prevalence p — and calibrated it against empirical power by simulation across three data-generating mechanisms and four group-size configurations (60 points, 2 000 replicates each). Results Under ideal-normal data the closed form was accurate to 0.009; under skew and dropout contamination it over-estimated the detection limit by up to 0.086, erring on the safe side in all eight non-normal configurations. Although treatment-induced senescence (TIS) effectively suppresses cancer cell proliferation, the long-term accumulation of the immunosuppressive senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) promotes immune evasion, leading to the failure of immunotherapy. Herein, a liposomal nanoparticle (T-Lipo@Das/Ber) encapsulating the ATR inhibitor Berzosertib and the Src/Bcr-Abl inhibitor Dasatinib was designed, which can target prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). T-Lipo@Das/Ber efficiently enters cells via PSMA-mediated endocytosis. On the one hand, Berzosertib inhibits ATR, increases DNA damage, and induces the release of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory factors via the cGAS-STING pathway, ultimately enhancing tumor immunogenicity. On the other hand, by inhibiting the Src/Bcr-Abl pathway, Dasatinib reprograms the SASP, reducing the secretion of immunosuppressive factors while promoting the exposure of calreticulin (CRT) and the release of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), thereby synergistically recruiting and activating immune cells. With the stimulation of both innate and adaptive immune responses, "immune cold tumor" is transformed into "immune hot tumor". When combined with αPD-1, it not only effectively inhibits the growth of the primary tumor, but also induces long-term immune memory to prevent tumor recurrence.

records.title: Steroid Hormone Receptor Isoform Diversity in Gynecologic Oncogenesis: Mechanisms, Biomarker Evidence, and Implications for Precision Oncology.
affiliations: Division of Cancer Research and Therapeutics, Yenepoya Research Centre, Yenepoya (Deemed to be University), Mangalore 575018, India.
records.abstract: Aberrant regulation of steroid hormone receptors (SHRs) can alter transcriptional programs relevant to gynecologic tumor initiation, progression, and treatment response. Importantly, receptor diversity arises through biologically distinct mechanisms, including alternative pre-mRNA splicing, alternative promoter usage, alternative translation initiation, and post-translational modification; receptor subtypes encoded by different genes should not be considered splice variants. This narrative review focuses on estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), androgen receptor (AR), glucocorticoid receptor (GR), and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) diversity in ovarian, endometrial, cervical, vulvar, and related gynecologic malignancies. Evidence is organized by tumor type and interpreted according to its level of support, distinguishing mechanistic preclinical observations from patient associations, candidate biomarkers, and clinically evaluated therapeutic strategies. Breast-cancer studies are used only as comparative mechanistic context when directly relevant to SHR isoform biology. Current evidence is strongest for ER- and PR-related receptor forms, whereas gynecologic data for AR, GR, and especially MR variants remain limited. Clarifying the molecular origin, tumor-specific function, and clinical validation of individual receptor forms will be essential before isoform-directed approaches can be incorporated into precision gynecologic oncology.

records.title: Truncating variants reveal functional divergence of the SAMD9 and SAMD9L paralogues.
affiliations: Department of Medicine Huddinge, Center for Hematology and Regenerative Medicine, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden.
records.abstract: Germline gain-of-function (GoF) variants in the paralogous sterile alpha motif domain containing 9 (SAMD9) and SAMD9-like (SAMD9L) genes cause myelodysplasia, primary immunodeficiencies, and neurological disorders. Predicting the functional consequences of individual variants, however, remains challenging, owing partly to the complexity of these large, multidomain proteins. Here, we functionally characterized several rare patient-derived SAMD9/9L variants, identifying multiple novel GoF and loss-of-function (LoF) variants, including SAMD9L p.C883X-the shortest documented SAMD9L GoF truncation within the NTPase domain. SAMD9L NTPase domain truncations are associated with severe, early-onset pathology, yet despite the high structural and sequence similarity between the two proteins, analogous truncating variants have not been reported in SAMD9 patients. To examine whether this reflects a fundamental difference, we generated multiple homologous SAMD9 truncations, which, unlike their SAMD9L counterparts, exhibited LoF rather than GoF activity. Additionally, established computational pathogenicity predictors failed to identify pathogenic variants or distinguish GoF from LoF. Collectively, these results demonstrate that functional outcomes in SAMD9/9L cannot be reliably inferred from sequence, structure, or computational prediction alone, underscoring the importance of empirical characterization.

records.title: Prospective Multicenter Evaluation of a Novel Low-Axial-Force Colonic Stent for Malignant Colorectal Obstruction.
affiliations: Division of Surgery, Gastrointestinal Center Yokohama Shin-Midori General Hospital Kanagawa Japan.
records.abstract: Objectives Self-expandable metal stents (SEMSs) are used as a bridge to surgery (BTS) or for palliation (PAL) in malignant colorectal obstruction, but high axial force may contribute to perforation. We prospectively evaluated the efficacy and safety of the low-axial-force Naturfit colonic stent in both settings. Methods This prospective multicenter single-arm study enrolled 208 patients at 11 Japanese institutions between 2019 and 2022 (BTS, n = 137; PAL, n = 71). The primary endpoint was clinical success of colorectal stenting; secondary endpoints included technical success, adverse events, surgical outcomes after BTS stenting, and 12-month palliative outcomes. Results Technical success and clinical success of colorectal stenting were both 99.0%, with perforation in three patients (1.4%). In the BTS cohort, clinical success of BTS was 97.1%; no perforations occurred, and early and late adverse-event rates were 1.5% and 3.7%. All patients underwent elective surgery; colostomy and laparoscopic surgery rates were 4.4% and 87.6%. In the palliative cohort, clinical success of colorectal stenting was 98.6%, late adverse events occurred in 16.9%, and 12-month overall survival and stent patency were 46.6% and 67.6%. Conclusions Naturfit achieved high technical and clinical success of colorectal stenting with a low perforation rate. These findings support its feasibility for malignant colorectal obstruction in both BTS and palliative settings, although comparative studies are needed

records.title: Engineering copper homeostasis for microenvironment-adaptive therapy in inflammation-driven disorders.
affiliations: Department of Clinical Pharmacology, Hunan Key Laboratory of Pharmacogenetics, National Clinical Research Center for Geriatric Disorders, Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha, 410008, PR China.
records.abstract: Inflammation-driven disorders (IDDs) arise from distinct initiating events, yet many persist because immune activation, oxidative and metabolic stress, regulated cell death, and tissue remodeling form self-reinforcing local niches. Copper connects these processes through its roles as a cuproenzyme cofactor, redox-active species and dynamically trafficked regulatory metal. Its therapeutic significance, however, is determined by disease stage, cell type, subcellular distribution and chemical state. Copper deficiency, excess or mislocalization may therefore be adaptive, protective or pathogenic in different contexts. This review develops a disease- and copper-state-specific framework that links copper homeostasis to therapeutic platform design. We first examine inflammation-associated remodeling of copper trafficking and compare representative copper states in autoimmune joint disease, metabolic inflammation, fibrosis, inflammation-associated cancer and infection-associated tissue repair. We then critically evaluate copper-dependent and copper-sensitive mechanisms governing inflammatory mediator availability, immune-cell programming and checkpoint regulation, regulated cell death, angiogenesis and stromal remodeling, while distinguishing direct mechanistic evidence from model-dependent inference. records.title: A fluorinated poly(amino acid) nanovaccine with spatiotemporally encoded innate priming and antigen cross-presentation for tumor immunotherapy.
affiliations: Key Laboratory of Polymer Chemistry and Physics of Ministry of Education, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Peking University, Beijing, 100871, China.
records.abstract: The efficacy of cancer vaccines depends on spatiotemporally coordinated innate immune priming and antigen cross-presentation, but this hierarchy remains difficult to control with existing delivery platforms. Here, we report a fluorinated diethylenetriamine-modified poly(aspartic acid) nanovaccine platform, termed DET-F, and identify DET-F30 as the optimized formulation for antigen delivery and immune activation. Perfluorooctyl side chains promote early endosomal toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) associated innate immune signaling and dendritic cell maturation, whereas the pH-responsive polymer backbone facilitates subsequent endosomal escape and cytosolic antigen release. This chemically encoded sequence enables delayed yet enhanced antigen cross-presentation in mature dendritic cells. DET-F30/antigen nanoparticles display efficient antigen loading and cellular uptake, activate TLR3-related innate immune pathways, and elicit robust antigen-specific CD8 + T cell immunity. In multiple tumor models, DET-F30-based vaccination suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, prolongs survival, and enhances post-surgical anti-PD-1 therapy. This work establishes fluorinated poly(amino acid)s as minimalist self-adjuvant nanovaccine vectors and demonstrates that precise polymer-architecture encoding can orchestrate sequential innate immune activation and antigen processing for improved cancer immunotherapy.

records.title: Acute Pancreatitis Caused by Impaction of Migrated Surgical Staples in the Duodenal Papilla After Distal Pancreatectomy.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology Oita Red Cross Hospital Oita Japan.
records.abstract: A 67-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy for pancreatic body cancer. On postoperative day (POD) 23, the patient presented with epigastric pain and was diagnosed with delayed peripancreatic fluid collection, which was treated with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage. On POD 51, the patient developed recurrent epigastric pain. Laboratory tests revealed elevated pancreatic enzyme and inflammatory marker levels. Computed tomography revealed acute pancreatitis and a high-density area in the duodenal papilla suggestive of a foreign body. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography revealed that the surgical staples were impacted in the minor duodenal papilla and were successfully removed. Although pancreatography did not demonstrate residual staples, three additional staples were subsequently removed from the pancreatic duct. Pancreatitis improved after endoscopic treatment, and the patient was discharged. This case suggests that the migration of staples used during surgery may be a contributing factor to postoperative pancreatitis.

records.abstract: Purpose To report long-term tumor control, toxicity, and functional outcomes after a second course of fractionated radiation therapy for recurrent craniopharyngioma previously treated with radiation therapy. Reirradiation was delivered to 54 Gy in 30 fractions with full overlap of the initial target; dose constraints to optic nerves, chiasm, and brainstem were Dmax/D0.03cc (Maximum Dose or Dose to 0.03 cubic centimetres) ≤54 Gy. Median follow-up after reirradiation was 4.1 years (range, 0.4-8.8). At the last follow-up, 4 patients were alive, all with local disease control (2 with radiological regression, 2 with stable disease). Two deaths occurred (1 due to progressive disease and 1 due to functional decline with stable imaging). records.abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. records.title: Beyond geographic access: Rural disparities in gynecologic oncology across the care continuum.
affiliations: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Carle Health, 611 W Park St, Urbana, IL 61801, USA.
records.abstract: Rural patients in the United States face disproportionate gynecologic cancer mortality compared to urban patients, driven by overlapping geographic, socioeconomic, and structural barriers that vary across cancer types and the care continuum. This review synthesizes the literature on rural disparities in cervical, endometrial, and ovarian cancers from prevention through survivorship. Rurality is defined variably across the literature, most commonly using government classification systems such as Rural-Urban Continuum Codes or Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. Rural women experience lower Human Papillomavirus vaccination rates and reduced uptake of guideline-concordant cervical cancer screening, higher rates of late-stage ovarian cancer diagnosis, and delayed endometrial cancer diagnosis. Even when rural patients access subspecialist care, treatment quality gaps persist, including higher rates of open surgical staging for endometrial cancer and reduced access to brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer. Survival disparities remain even among rural patients treated at tertiary centers with subspecialist involvement, underscoring that geographic access alone is insufficient. Insurance status, health literacy, financial hardship, and limited social support compound these barriers throughout the continuum. affiliations: Department of Oral Diagnostic and Surgical Sciences Faculty of Dentistry University of Otago Dunedin New Zealand.
records.abstract: This review examines the current literature on the application of atomic force microscopy (AFM) to cancer mechanophenotyping, with particular emphasis on cellular Young's modulus and its potential diagnostic significance. A structured electronic search of PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar was conducted to identify studies published between 1999 and 2025 reporting AFM-based measurements of cellular Young's modulus in cancer-related models. Across multiple malignancies, reduced cellular stiffness is frequently observed in malignant compared with non-malignant cells and is associated with cytoskeletal remodelling, increased deformability and altered cell-matrix interactions. However, the relationship between Young's modulus and malignancy is not universally monotonic. Nanomechanical properties may vary across different pathological states and malignant phenotypes rather than following a simple monotonic trajectory, while invasive and metastatic cells can dynamically remodel their cytoskeleton and modify their stiffness in response to environmental and mechanical constraints. Young's modulus should therefore not be regarded as an isolated universal cancer biomarker, but rather as one component of a dynamic mechanophenotype influenced by disease stage, cellular region, microenvironment and measurement methodology. records.abstract: The molecular mechanism of changing and varied antigenicity of membrane proteins during cancerogenesis, where changes in membrane lipid composition and abiotic tumor microenvironment occur regularly, is unknown. By challenging ovarian cancer cells to tumorigenic hypoxia and acidosis, we observed unexpected surface exposure of the Na + -dependent phosphate transporter (NaPi2b) N-termini (NT) previously hidden on the cytoplasmic side of "resting" cancer cells in the accordance with its predicted orientation, violating the Positive Inside Rule. Consistently with the Charge Balance Rule of membrane protein assembly, the reorientation of NaPi2b NT coincides with loss of asymmetry and surface exposure of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), while the coincident exposure of PE and NT of NaPi2b is prevented by knockdown of phospholipid scramblase 1 (PLSCR1). These dynamic topological events can lead to unmasking of previously hidden extramembrane domains (epitopes), which can be potentially used as a novel target for targeted anti-tumor immunotherapy.
