records.title: Disrupting the cholesterol-mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma.
affiliations: Key Laboratory of Microbial Pathogenesis and Interventions of Fujian Province University, Biomedical Research Center of South China, College of Life Sciences, Fujian Normal University, 1 Keji Road, Fuzhou, 350117, China.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor-stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol-mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo , FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

records.title: Parthenolide reduces transgelin-2 expression in inhibiting glioblastoma malignancy through activating GSK3β-suppressing CREB signaling.
affiliations: Department of Neurosurgery, Taipei City Hospital Ren-Ai Branch, Taipei, Taiwan.
records.abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a WHO grade IV brain tumor with aggressive growth and frequent recurrence, and temozolomide (TMZ) remains the standard first-line chemotherapy despite limited durable benefits. Parthenolide (Pt), a sesquiterpene lactone derived from the medicinal plant feverfew, has shown antitumor activity in multiple cancer types; however, its therapeutic potential and downstream mechanisms in GBM have not been fully defined. Herein, we demonstrate that Pt induces apoptosis, suppresses stemness, and reduces invasion in human U-87MG and T98G cells. Pt also potentiates TMZ's efficacy in vitro and in an orthotopic GBM model with male NOD-SCID mice. RNA-sequencing and pathway analyses revealed that Pt markedly represses epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated programs. Among the most significantly downregulated genes, transgelin-2 (TAGLN2) emerged as a key Pt-responsive target, and its high expression was correlated with poor survival in glioma cohorts. TAGLN2 overexpression rescued Pt-mediated suppression of malignant phenotypes and the EMT, supporting a functional role for TAGLN2 in Pt responsiveness. Mechanistically, inhibitor screening identified glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β) as a critical upstream regulator of Pt-induced TAGLN2 repression. records.title: Cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot enabling ultrasensitive one-pot detection of dual miRNAs in triple-negative breast cancer.
affiliations: Department of Clinical Laboratory, Ganzhou People's Hospital, Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, 341000, China. Electronic address: yuluhu@163.com.
records.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are critical biomarkers for the early diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but sensitive simultaneous detection of multiple miRNAs remains a clinical challenge. Herein, we report an innovative biosensing method based on a cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot for one-pot, rapid, and ultrasensitive dual miRNA detection. Target miRNAs trigger the cascade DNA walker, which integrates catalytic hairpin assembly and enzyme-mediated strand displacement, to generate abundant single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). These ssDNA then activate the photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot under light illumination, enabling amplified fluorescence signaling for dual-target quantification. The assay exhibits a linear range of 100 aM to 1 pM with a limit of detection of 48.7 aM. Serum recovery experiments and cell line tests confirm its reliability in complex matrices. Clinical validation using 30 plasma samples (15 TNBC patients, 15 healthy controls) demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve, AUC = 0.964). This method features simple operation and strong clinical translational potential, offering a reliable tool for the early diagnosis of TNBC.

records.abstract: Background The combination of ultra hypofractionated radiotherapy (U-HFRT) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has been proposed to increase systemic anti-tumor response, but the incidence of toxicity after concomitant ICI and U-HFRT remains to be explored. Methods We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of the incidence of adverse events (AEs) after concomitant ICI and U-HFRT in prospective trials, to evaluate whether ICI and U-HFRT were more toxic than ICI monotherapy. The primary outcome was the incidence of selected National Cancer Institute Common Toxicity Criteria of Adverse Events (CTCAE) of any grade and grade 3-4 (G3-4). Secondary outcomes were median overall survival (mOS) and median progression-free survival (mPFS). records.title: Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen-Targeted Radioligand Therapy in Prostate Cancer: Patient Selection, Treatment Workflow, and Emerging Directions.
affiliations: Department of Nuclear Medicine, Adiyaman University Research and Training Hospital, Adiyaman, Turkey. Electronic address: dilaradenizmen@istanbul.edu.tr.
records.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted theranostics have become an important component of advanced prostate cancer management by integrating molecular imaging with radioligand therapy. This review summarizes the biologic rationale for PSMA targeting, the role of PSMA PET in patient selection, and the clinical evidence supporting PSMA-directed radioligand therapy. Practical aspects of treatment administration, toxicity monitoring, response assessment, and sequencing are discussed, together with emerging strategies involving novel ligands, alpha emitters, dosimetry, and combination approaches.

records.title: FDG PET/CT in Gynecologic Malignancies.
affiliations: Department of Nuclear Medicine, Istanbul University, Istanbul Faculty of Medicine, Fatih, Istanbul 34093, Turkey. Electronic address: aslanerkubra@istanbul.edu.tr.
records.abstract: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT has become an essential complementary modality in the management of gynecologic malignancies, combining metabolic and anatomic information beyond the morphologic limitations of CT and MRI. This review examines its clinical roles and diagnostic limitations across cervical, endometrial, ovarian, vulvar, and vaginal cancers, focusing on nodal staging, recurrence detection, treatment response assessment, and prognostication. Its distinct strengths-nodal staging in cervical cancer and recurrence detection in endometrial and ovarian cancers-are highlighted alongside key interpretive pitfalls. Emerging approaches, including PET/MRI, volumetric parameters, FAPI and other novel radiopharmaceuticals, and radiomics, are discussed as future directions in gynecologic oncology.

records.title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review.
affiliations: New Technologies Research Centre, University of West Bohemia in Pilsen, 30100, Pilsen, Czech Republic.
records.abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

records.title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
affiliations: Institute of Tissue Regeneration Engineering (ITREN), Dankook University, Cheonan, 31116, Republic of Korea.
records.abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. records.title: Inhaled nanogels ameliorate vascular remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension <i>via</i> normalization of endothelia-smooth muscle cell crosstalk.
affiliations: Basic Medical Research Center, The Third Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, Changzhou, 213003, China.
records.abstract: Maintaining appropriate vascular nitric oxide (NO) levels in pulmonary arteries is crucial for the alleviation of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). However, in the injured vascular microenvironment, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) deplete NO to generate peroxynitrite, which aggravates the oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction. Herein, ROS-responsive, zwitterionic nanogels (NGs), containing arginine pendants as NO precursors and encapsulating resveratrol (RSV) as an anti-oxidant, were developed for PAH management via inhalation. Benefiting from their zwitterionic surface that repels mucin adsorption, the inhaled NGs exhibit effective pulmonary mucus penetration and mucosal absorption, enabling robust diffusion to the injured pulmonary arteries. In the oxidative vascular microenvironment, the diselenide crosslinkers within the NGs are cleaved, promoting NGs dissociation and on-demand RSV release. The released RSV scavenges ROS and the arginine pendants are oxidized to generate NO, which cooperate to interrupt the ROS/NO disequilibrium. In a hypoxia/SU5416-induced PAH mouse model, inhaled NGs efficiently alleviate vascular remodeling and reduce pulmonary arterial pressure. This study offers an effective strategy for pulmonary drug delivery, and holds promising potentials for the management of PAH.

records.title: Successful Management of a Completely Disconnected Bile Leak After Hepatectomy Using Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Transluminal Drainage of a Biloma: A Case Report.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology Osaka Rosai Hospital Sakai Japan.
records.abstract: Post-hepatectomy bile leak is a common postoperative complication. It usually resolves spontaneously but may be refractory. In cases of completely disconnected bile ducts, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)-guided drainage is often technically difficult, and invasive additional procedures may be required. We report a completely disconnected bile leak after hepatectomy successfully treated with endoscopic ultrasound-guided transluminal drainage (EUS-TD) after unsuccessful EUS-guided biliary drainage (EUS-BD). A 78-year-old woman underwent anterior sectionectomy for recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma and developed persistent bile leakage. ERCP showed complete disruption of the right posterior sectoral bile duct, and guidewire passage was impossible. EUS-BD failed because of the nondilated bile duct; therefore, the bile leak-associated infected biloma was drained through an endoscopically created route under EUS guidance. The infected biloma showed significant shrinkage, and the patient was discharged without complications. EUS-TD may represent an alternative therapeutic option for completely disconnected bile leaks when EUS-BD is technically difficult.

Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. records.abstract: The mechanical properties of tumor cells critically influence their invasive behavior, yet how extracellular viscosity regulates cellular deformation-recovery dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we developed time-delay deformation cytometry, a microfluidic platform integrating inertial focusing, hydrodynamic deformation, and sequential imaging to characterize single-cell mechanical responses and morphological recovery. Using glioblastoma models exposed to elevated extracellular viscosity, we identified a distinct mechanical phenotype characterized by increased deformation resistance and incomplete morphological recovery within the millisecond observation window. Complementary atomic force microscopy measurements revealed increased cellular stiffness and Young's modulus, accompanied by reduced mechanical hysteresis, supporting viscosity-associated mechanical reinforcement. Notably, this altered recovery phenotype was associated with enhanced cellular invasion. records.title: Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
affiliations: Nursing Department, Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital Zhejiang University School of Medicine Hangzhou China.
records.abstract: Background Although many predictive models have been developed or validated for delayed bleeding after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), their methodological quality and clinical utility remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed and critically appraised all available predictive models for this outcome. Methods We searched five databases through March 2026 for observational studies that developed or validated prediction models or scoring systems for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD in adults (≥18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST. Results Of 25,177 records screened, five studies reporting five predictive models were included. The incidence of delayed bleeding ranged from 2.9% to 9.9%. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation areas under the curve [AUCs] ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. All studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, mainly because of inadequate reporting in the predictor, outcome, and analysis domains, although most had low concerns regarding applicability. Conclusions This systematic review identified five predictive models for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD. Lesion location and size were the most frequently reported predictors. records.title: Thermosensitive and tumor-targeted asparaginase fusion protein enables metabolic-immunotherapy for solid tumors.
affiliations: Beijing Advanced Center of Cellular Homeostasis and Aging-Related Diseases, The Center of Biomedical Engineering, Institute of Advanced Clinical Medicine, Peking University, Beijing, 100191, China; State Key Laboratory of Natural and Biomimetic Drugs, Beijing Key Laboratory of Molecular Pharmaceutics and New Drug Delivery, School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Peking University, Beijing, 100191, China; Peking University-Yunnan Baiyao International Medical Research Center, Peking University International Cancer Institute, Beijing, 100191, China; Institute of Medical Technology, Peking University Health Science Center, Beijing, 100191, China.
records.abstract: Metabolic therapies targeting tumor amino acid dependence, represented by asparaginase (ASNase), have shown limited efficacy in solid tumors, owing to poor stability, low penetration, and high immunogenicity. Here, we design a thermosensitive tumor-targeted ASNase fusion protein (ASNase-ELP-LHRH) via AlphaFold2, by integrating elastin-like polypeptide (ELP) and luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH), to overcome these drawbacks. ELP drives in situ depot formation, extending half-life to ∼400 h (95-fold increase) and reducing anti-ASNase antibody levels 70-fold. LHRH mediates receptor-dependent tumor targeting and deep penetration. ASNase-ELP-LHRH achieves persistent asparagine (Asn) depletion, counteracting metabolic adaptation to induce nutrient starvation and apoptosis. Mechanistically, the construct blocks metastasis by suppressing epithelial-mesenchymal transition through downregulating Twist1 and upregulating E-cadherin, effectively inhibiting lung metastasis for 25 days in triple-negative breast cancer models. We further observed time-dependent changes in CD8 + T-cell effector-marker expression under Asn deprivation, characterized by dynamic alterations in IFN-γ and granzyme B expression. Combined with anti-PD-L1, this achieves a "dual boost" of antitumor immunity, durably inhibiting metastasis for 40 days and extending survival 1.5-fold. affiliations: Department of Health Technology and Informatics, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hung Hom, Kowloon, Hong Kong SAR, China.
records.abstract: Objectives Radiation-induced hypothyroidism (RIHT) is a common late toxicity after head and neck radiotherapy. We aimed to develop and externally validate a multimodal Cox model for patient-specific cumulative RIHT risk assessment. Materials & methods This retrospective multicentre study included 1407 patients across four cohorts. The model was developed in the training cohort and externally validated in three independent cohorts. Candidate predictors included CT radiomics, dosiomics, dose-volume histogram parameters, and clinical variables. A multimodal Cox model was developed and used to estimate cumulative risks across time horizons. Temporal risk groups were derived from predicted 3- and 7-year risks. Results A total of 1407 patients (mean age, 55.4 ± 13.8 years; 1027 men) were evaluated and RIHT occurred in 694 (49.3%). The final model integrated three CT radiomics features, four dosiomics features, mean thyroid dose, age and N stage. It achieved C-index/overall AUC values of 0.714/0.765 in the development cohort and 0.725/0.800, 0.680/0.754, and 0.627/0.690 in the three external validation cohorts. records.title: Prostate Cancer and PSMA PET/CT.
affiliations: Department of Nuclear Medicine, Istanbul University, Istanbul Faculty of Medicine, Fatih, Istanbul 34093, Turkey. Electronic address: begum.arca@istanbul.edu.tr.
records.abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/computed tomography (CT) in the management of prostate cancer. It explores the physiologic biodistribution of various 68 Ga and 18F-labeled tracers, standardized imaging protocols, and essential diagnostic criteria. We detail the modality's transformative role in primary staging, localizing biochemical recurrence at low prostate-specific antigen levels, and selecting patients for radioligand therapy. By highlighting critical diagnostic pitfalls and the emerging challenge of PSMA-negative disease, this article equips clinicians with the practical knowledge necessary to integrate PSMA PET/CT effectively into multidisciplinary oncology practice.

records.title: Thyroid Disease in the Era of Obesity and Glucagon-Like-Peptide-1 Agonists.
affiliations: Department of Otolaryngology, University of Texas Medical Branch, Galveston, TX, USA. Electronic address: orcoblen@UTMB.EDU.
records.abstract: The thyroid gland plays a critical role in regulating metabolism. Dysfunctions in the thyroid gland are closely associated with alterations in body mass index. The relationship between thyroid disease and obesity is complex and bidirectional with hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism influencing body weight. In the last decade, there has been an increase in the incidence of thyroid cancer as well as the prevalence of obesity. Emerging weight loss therapies and their potential association with thyroid malignancy remains an active area of investigation. Additionally, important perioperative and surgical considerations must be addressed in patients undergoing thyroidectomy.

affiliations: Thayer School of Engineering, Dartmouth College, Hanover, NH, United States.
records.abstract: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a debilitating sequela of radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck cancer (HNC), characterized by persistent bone exposure or radiographic non-viability and profound tissue repair failure. Despite advances in radiation delivery and clinical management, ORN remains challenging to treat, with therapeutic strategies largely focused on symptom control, infection mitigation, or surgical reconstruction rather than restoration of regenerative capacity. Emerging evidence suggests that radiation-induced cellular senescence represents a central and underrecognized driver of ORN pathophysiology. Ionizing radiation disrupts the bone microenvironment through sustained vascular injury, impaired osteogenic-angiogenic coupling, chronic inflammation, and the accumulation of senescent bone-resident and stromal cells that secrete a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Together, these changes create a hostile niche that suppresses bone remodeling and wound healing long after radiation exposure. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. We further propose senotherapeutic strategies targeting radiation-induced cellular senescence as a complementary and potentially transformative avenue to restore tissue repair capacity. records.title: Psychoneuroimmunology of glioblastoma: How emotional states shape tumor biology.
affiliations: Laboratory of Design and Drug Synthesis (LPSF), Nucleus of Research in Therapeutic Innovation Suely Galdino (NUPIT-SG), Biosciences Center, Federal University of Pernambuco, Recife, Brazil; Laboratory of Immunomodulation and New Therapeutic Approaches (LINAT), Nucleus of Research in Therapeutic Innovation Suely Galdino (NUPIT-SG), Biosciences Center, Federal University of Pernambuco, Recife, Brazil.
records.abstract: Psychological states profoundly influence physiological processes, with growing evidence linking emotional dysregulation to cancer progression. Within the framework of psychoneuroimmunology, recent findings have shown that chronic stress, depression and anxiety disrupt immune surveillance and promote a pro-inflammatory environment that favors tumor growth. Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the most aggressive brain tumor, appears particularly sensitive to these neuroimmune influences. Some stress mediators and neurotransmitters-such as glucocorticoids and catecholamines- modulate the GBM microenvironment, fostering tumor-supportive pathways and epigenetic changes. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence connecting emotional disturbances and glioma biology, highlighting shared neuroimmune mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that integrating psychosocial and neuropharmacological strategies into GBM care could improve patients outcomes by targeting both tumor biology and emotional well-being.

records.abstract: Type-I hypersensitivity is a mast cell-mediated degranulation process induced by IgE-antigen recognition. Inspired by this highly specific mechanism, we developed a new cell therapy platform by genetically engineering mouse mast cell line MC/9 to overexpress the cytotoxic proteins perforin and granzyme B (PG-MCs) via lentiviral transduction. In the melanoma model utilizing B16 cells expressing membrane-bound OVA, a polarized degranulation of mast cells towards cancer cells was validated upon the recognition of antigens by anti-OVA IgE. PG-MCs could selectively kill cancer cells via IgE-antigen recognition. The IgE-sensitized PG-MCs administered through an intertumoral route delivered perforin 1 (Prf1) and granzyme B (Gmzb) toward target cells to potentiate anti-tumor efficacy. Moreover, we demonstrated the reprogramming effect of tumor microenvironment by PG-MC-induced hypersensitivity, driving an immune remodeling of the tumor milieu, characterized by the increased lymphocyte infiltration. In addition, this mast cell therapy, in combination with 5- fluorouracil (5-Fu), induced a significant inhibition of tumor growth in a B16-OVA mouse model, which is associated with the depletion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs).

records.abstract: Objectives Small colorectal polyps sometimes include high-grade adenomas or carcinomas that require endoscopic resection with electrocautery. records.abstract: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is an important biomarker for prostate cancer (PCa) screening, but conventional detection methods rely on sophisticated instruments and centralized laboratories. Herein, we developed an aggregation-induced emission fluorescent microsphere-based lateral flow immunoassay strip (AIEFM-LFIS) for rapid and quantitative detection of PSA. Highly specific anti-PSA monoclonal antibodies were prepared by hybridoma technology and conjugated with AIEFMs to construct fluorescent immunoprobes, which were further integrated with a portable LumiS-1 Pro reader for quantitative signal acquisition and smartphone-based data transmission. Under optimized conditions, PSA could be detected within 20 min over a detection range of 0.5-62.5 ng/mL, with a limit of detection of 0.28 ng/mL. Clinical evaluation of 40 serum samples showed a sensitivity of 96.2%, a specificity of 100%, and a consistency of 97.5% with chemiluminescence immunoassay. Owing to its high sensitivity, portability, intelligent quantitative readout, and low cost, the developed platform provides a promising tool for decentralized PSA testing and preliminary PCa screening in primary healthcare and resource-limited settings.

affiliations: Key Laboratory of Functional Polymer Materials of Ministry of Education, Institute of Polymer Chemistry, State Key Laboratory of Medicinal Chemical Biology, Frontiers Science Center for New Organic Matter, Haihe Laboratory of Sustainable Chemical Transformations, College of Chemistry, Nankai University, Tianjin, 300071, China.
records.abstract: T cell-based cancer immunotherapies have transformed oncology; however, their clinical benefit remains limited in immunologically cold tumors, where poor T cell infiltration and impaired effector function weaken endogenous tumor cell killing. Here, we developed GrB@A-nChap, a cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)-inspired nanotherapeutic that chaperones granzyme B (GrB) into the tumor cell cytosol to supplement deficient cytotoxic effector activity in "cold" tumors. Mechanistically, GrB@A-nChap protects GrB under physiological conditions, undergoes partial protonation in the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment to enhance tumor cell uptake, and further responds to lysosomal acidity to promote acidity-dependent lysosomal escape and cytosolic GrB release. Cytosolic GrB then induces mitochondrial dysfunction, caspase-3 activation, and GSDME cleavage, thereby triggering an apoptosis-pyroptosis cascade. This cell death process is accompanied by ICD-associated molecular signals and enhanced dendritic cell maturation. In vivo , GrB@A-nChap treatment was associated with increased intratumoral immune cell infiltration and local immune modulation and enhanced the therapeutic response to αPD-1 treatment. This work establishes a CTLinspired nanotherapeutic that enables cytosolic GrB delivery and provides cell independent GrB-mediated tumor cell killing, offering a potential strategy for complementing existing treatments for cold tumors.

records.title: USF1 promotes growth and glycolysis in acute myeloid leukemia cells.
affiliations: Department of Immunology, Basic Medical School, Guizhou Medical University, Guiyang, Guizhou, 561113, China.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a hematological malignancy characterized by impaired hematopoiesis and aggressive progression, with limited treatment options and poor prognosis, especially in elderly patients. Metabolic reprogramming, particularly enhanced glycolysis, is a hallmark of AML and contributes to disease progression and therapy resistance. Upstream stimulatory factor 1 (USF1) regulates metabolism, the cell cycle, and oncogenesis in solid tumors, whereas its role in AML remains unclear. Herein, we investigated the role and underlying mechanism of USF1 in regulating USP25 transcription and promoting AML progression. We found that USF1 was highly expressed in AML samples and cell lines, and its elevated expression was associated with poor prognosis. Functional assays showed that USF1 promoted AML cell growth and glycolysis while inhibiting apoptosis. Mechanistically, USF1 directly bound to the USP25 promoter, enhancing its transcription. Knockdown of USP25 reversed the tumor-promoting effects of USF1. Moreover, in vivo studies demonstrated that silencing USF1 significantly inhibited tumor growth. In conclusion, USF1 promotes AML cell growth and glycolysis through the transcriptional activation of USP25, thereby identifying the USF1-USP25 axis as a potential therapeutic target for AML.

records.title: Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series.
affiliations: Wolfson Unit for Endoscopy, St Mark's The National Bowel Hospital London UK.
records.abstract: Flushing endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a refinement of saline immersion ESD in which energy-synchronized saline flushing from the knife tip is hypothesized to disperse micro-bubbles and facilitate more controlled coagulation at the tissue interface. We retrospectively evaluated the technical feasibility of this approach in 10 rectal procedures performed at a tertiary referral center. Complete procedural videos were reviewed to describe treated visible submucosal vessel burden, minor bleeding, episodes of transient loss of visualization, and hemostatic forceps use. En bloc and histologically margin-negative (R0) resection was achieved in all 10 cases, while curative endoscopic resection was achieved in nine cases (90%). No intraprocedural perforation, delayed bleeding, post-ESD coagulation syndrome, or unplanned repeat intervention occurred. Median lesion size was 55 mm (interquartile range, 40-69.5), median procedure duration was 102.5 min (100-167.5), and median treated visible vessel count was 21 (11.5-40.75), corresponding to 1.04 vessels/cm 2 (0.64-1.74). Minor bleeding and transient loss of visualization occurred during procedures but were controlled endoscopically. Hemostatic forceps were required therapeutically for active bleeding from one vessel across the series, and no procedure required abandonment or conversion to surgery. records.abstract: In head and neck imaging somatostatin receptor (SSTR) imaging with DOTATATE has markedly improved detection of meningiomas compared to schwannomas as well as preoperative surgical or radiation therapy planning and posttreatment surveillance. DOTATATE is useful in identifying multiple paragangliomas especially if hereditary, multiple endocrine tumors in genetic syndromes and medullary thyroid cancer and may potentially assessment of middle ear adenomas, pituitary neuroendocrine tumors and olfactory neuroblastoma. SSTR PET may help predict response to targeted tumor treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy.

records.title: Clinical Outcomes of Double Half-Pigtail Versus Straight Plastic Stents for Endoscopic Biliary Drainage of Malignant Distal Biliary Obstruction.
affiliations: Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatology Saga Medical Center Koseikan Saga Japan.
records.abstract: Objectives The clinical performance of double half-pigtail plastic stents (DHPs) for malignant distal biliary obstruction (MDBO) remains unclear. We compared DHPs with straight plastic stents (STs) regarding the timing, incidence, and causes of recurrent biliary obstruction (RBO). Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography-guided transpapillary single plastic stent placements for MDBO performed between October 2022 and March 2026. For the primary analysis, only initial stenting episodes were included. The primary endpoint was the time to RBO (TRBO), which was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and log-rank methods. Results A total of 131 stent-placement episodes in 86 patients were eligible. The primary analysis included 72 patients undergoing initial stenting, comprising 20 patients in the DHP group and 52 patients in the ST group. The DHP and ST groups had a similar median TRBO (116 vs. 119 days; log-rank p = 0.726), incidence of RBO (40.0% vs. 46.2%; p = 0.638), and incidence of stent occlusion (40.0% vs. 32.7%; p = 0.560). No migration occurred with DHPs, whereas seven migration events occurred with STs (0% vs. 13.5%; p = 0.084). Both groups had similar adverse event rates (0% vs. 11.5%; p = 0.113). Conclusions DHPs did not prolong the TRBO or reduce its incidence compared with STs. However, migration-related RBO occurred only with STs. The potential advantage of DHPs may be a lower incidence of stent migration

records.abstract: Cervical cancer, the fourth most frequent malignancy in women worldwide, continues to be a major public health concern. Around 90% of high-grade cervical cancer cases are linked to infection with human papillomavirus (HPV). This phenotype, histologically, includes two major subtypes of cervical cancer: squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma. Drug resistance poses a major hurdle to treatment because it targets the apoptotic pathway. To overcome this, there is an urgent need for alternative routes to a curative strategy. Here, we focused on identifying non-apoptotic cell death pathways as a potential therapeutic option. Bulk RNA sequencing data for cervical cancer samples were obtained from the TCGA-CESC dataset. We combined gene set enrichment analysis, co-expression network analysis, and machine learning, which revealed ferroptosis as a key vulnerability at the bulk RNA level. Single-cell RNA sequencing data further confirmed the expression of ferroptosis-related components, including SCC and ADC. Subsequent analyses focused on identifying key regulators of the ferroptosis pathway. Further dissection of ferroptosis regulators and PSAT1 was prioritized as a prime translational target in adenocarcinoma compared with squamous cell carcinoma. To advance therapeutic translation, we applied AI-driven de novo compound generation to design a candidate drug targeting PSAT1. Standard treatment involves surgical resection, followed by radiotherapy and chemotherapy with temozolomide (TMZ). However, resistance to treatment is frequently observed. PIMREG is a marker of proliferation highly expressed across different tumor types, with particularly elevated levels in GBM. Our previous study revealed that PIMREG silencing sensitizes GBM cells to TMZ treatment and affects ATM activation, a key apical kinase involved in DNA damage signaling. Here we assessed the functionally enriched pathways associated with high PIMREG expression in GBM patient samples, analyzed the interactome of PIMREG upon treatment of GBM cells with TMZ and evaluated the impact of PIMREG loss on DNA damage signaling, DNA break formation and the repair of double-strand breaks. Our findings reveal that PIMREG functions as a direct substrate for ATM/ATR kinases, interacts with key DNA repair proteins upon TMZ treatment and actively facilitates the cellular response to chemotherapy- and radiotherapy-induced DNA damage. affiliations: Department of Biochemistry, Faculty of Science, Ain Shams University, Abbassia, 11566, Cairo, Egypt.
records.abstract: Early diagnosis of ovarian cancer remains a major clinical challenge. Human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) has emerged as a promising biomarker for early OC detection. To address limitations of existing HE4 quantification methods, we developed a nano-optical biosensor based on a luminescent europium-thiosemicarbazide (Eu-TSC) complex immobilized within a modified epoxy-cellulose thin-film matrix. The Eu-TSC thin film exhibited characteristic europium excitation and emission bands at 395 nm and 617 nm. Following functionalization with a monoclonal anti-HE4 antibody, the biosensor displayed a concentration-dependent fluorescence quenching response upon HE4 binding. A linear analytical response was obtained over 0.05-0.37 ng mL -1 , with LOD of 0.108 ng mL -1 . However, the LOQ (0.327 ng mL -1 ) lies close to the upper limit of the linear range, the practical validated quantification interval is extremely narrow (approximately 0.327-0.37 ng mL -1 ). This interval is far too narrow to cover the clinical HE4 range, and the present sensor should therefore be regarded as a preliminary proof-of-concept platform rather than a clinically suitable quantitative assay. records.title: Management of Benign and Aggressive Bone Tumors of the Hand and Wrist.
affiliations: Department of Orthopedics, JR Tokyo General Hospital, Tokyo, Japan; Division of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, Mayo Clinic, Rochester, MN, USA.
records.abstract: Bone tumors of the hand and wrist are relatively uncommon, creating the clinical challenge of differentiating benign lesions like enchondromas, from locally aggressive tumors such as giant cell tumors of bone and more aggressive malignancies. The hand's complex anatomy complicates treatment, demanding precise, function-preserving surgery; fortunately, advances in imaging, targeted agents, and reconstruction have expanded treatment strategies to preserve function. This review provides surgeons with an overview of managing benign and aggressive bone tumors. Primary hand malignancies such as osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma require multidisciplinary management incorporating wide surgical resection, chemotherapy, and in select cases radiotherapy.

records.abstract: The diagnostic challenges linked to rare neurological diseases, including Glioblastoma, remain a significant issue, especially in resource-limited healthcare systems like India. Conventional deep learning algorithms work well for traditional medical imaging tasks, but rare disease datasets have data scarcity and an imbalance. This paper presents GOAT-NET (Glioblastoma, Oligodendroglioma, and Astrocytoma Tumor Network), a meta-learning-based diagnostic framework aimed at improving the categorisation of rare Glioblastoma and Healthy samples using a limited number of annotated MRI samples. It was primarily trained and validated on Astrocytoma, Oligodendroglioma, Glioblastoma, and Healthy classes. Additionally, GOAT-NET uses explainable AI methods like LIME and SHAP to make visual explanations that are easy to understand. The training and validation accuracy for the base model is 97.34% and 96.85% respectively. records.abstract: Effective biomarker detection is critical for timely and accurate clinical disease diagnosis. This review specifically focuses on transcriptional regulation-based biosensors, primarily those utilizing allosteric transcription factors (aTFs) and two-component systems (TCSs). By integrating these regulatory sensing modules into engineered microbial chassis, researchers can achieve continuous, real-time biomarker monitoring even within complex and otherwise inaccessible physiological environments. This review particularly focuses on microbial chassis rather than mammalian systems due to their highly tractable genetics, rapid response kinetics, and their unique potential to be deployed as autonomous living probiotics for in situ theranostics. Furthermore, coupling these sensors with engineered actuator genes enables the construction of intelligent therapeutic genetic circuits. records.title: Antifibrotic hydrogel strategies for scarless tissue regeneration: mechanisms, design, and application.
affiliations: School of Medicine and Health, MOE Key Laboratory of Micro-systems and Micro-structures Manufacturing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, 150080, China.
records.abstract: Tissue repair is a highly coordinated process, yet dysregulated fibrosis often diverts healing toward scar formation, resulting in permanent structural and functional impairment. Achieving scarless regeneration requires precise modulation of the wound microenvironment to support functional tissue reconstruction. Hydrogels, owing to their biocompatibility, tunable mechanics, and controllable delivery capabilities, have emerged as promising platforms for regenerative therapy. Recent multifunctional hydrogels can regulate tissue repair through microstructural engineering, mechanical modulation, immune regulation, pro-angiogenic stimulation, and dynamic extracellular matrix remodeling, thereby suppressing fibrotic progression. However, current reviews mainly focus on accelerating wound closure and lack systematic discussion of antifibrotic hydrogel design across different tissues. In this review, we summarize the key mechanisms underlying scar formation and propose design principles for hydrogel-mediated scarless regeneration. We further highlight recent advances in multiple tissues, including skin, tendon, cornea, urethra, nerve, endometrium, liver, myocardium, emphasizing both shared principles and tissue-specific requirements. Finally, we discuss translational challenges and future opportunities, particularly AI-driven hydrogel design for functional regeneration.

records.title: A transferrin receptor-targeted liposome for iron metabolism regulation-augmented photodynamic therapy in glioblastoma.
affiliations: Guangdong Key Laboratory for Biomedical Measurements and Ultrasound Imaging, Marshall Laboratory of Biomedical Engineering, International Cancer Center, Laboratory of Evolutionary Theranostics (LET), School of Biomedical Engineering, Shenzhen University Medical School, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen, 518055, China.
records.abstract: The clinical standard treatments for glioblastoma (GBM) present a therapeutic challenge of high recurrence. 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA)-based photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers a promising alternative owing to the selective biosynthesis of protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) in tumor mitochondria with favorable phototoxicity. However, the highly elevated iron metabolism leads to low biosynthetic efficiency and insufficient accumulation of PpIX, thus limiting the PDT efficacy. Here, we developed a transferrin receptor (TfR)-targeted liposome (AD@LST) that co-delivers 5-ALA and the iron chelator deferoxamine (DFO) for tumor-targeted PpIX biosynthesis and augmented PDT in GBM. records.title: Experimental evidence for the beneficial effects of low-concentration ozone.
affiliations: Department of Neurosciences, Biomedicine and Movement Sciences, University of Verona, Verona, Italy.
records.abstract: Ozone (O3), a molecule consisting of three oxygen atoms, is an unstable compound whose clinical application as a complementary therapy continues to expand. Although numerous clinical studies support its therapeutic potential, the molecular basis of its effects has remained poorly understood. This review summarizes the current knowledge on the cellular and molecular mechanisms activated by low-concentration O3. Central to its action is the induction of mild oxidative stress by low concentrations of O3, which triggers an antioxidant response mediated through nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2, enhancing cell survival. Additionally, low-concentration O3 exhibits antiinflammatory properties by modulating cytokine expression, inhibiting metalloproteinases, and activating macrophages. The regenerative potential of low-concentration O3 may be attributed to the stimulation of fibroblasts, chondrocytes, and osteoblasts. Moreover, the antitumor effects of low-concentration O3 in cancer cell lines and animal models appear to be linked to the inhibition of cell proliferation and migration, as well as proapoptotic activity. More research is needed to determine the best treatment methods, long-term effectiveness, and standardized clinical procedures for ozone therapy in specific diseases. This review provides a detailed reference for understanding how O3 therapy works.

affiliations: Department of Internal Medicine II, University Hospital Würzburg, Würzburg, Germany.
records.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a malignant plasma cell disease inducing osteolytic lesions by disrupting bone homeostasis, fostering catabolic and suppressing anabolic functions. While the impact on osteoblast generation and function is well documented, alterations of osteocyte function and extracellular matrix (ECM) are not yet fully understood. Thus, using a syngeneic mouse model of MM by injecting MOPC315.BM cells intratibially into BALB/c mice (n = 95), we performed transcriptomic profiling of an osteocyte-enriched population and identified a mechanosensitive matrisomal gene signature, which was disrupted by tumor engraftment. Four of these genes (Vegfa, Sdc1, Sema3a, Ccl2) were also load-responsive in a murine osteocyte (IDG-SW3 cells) bioreactor model. Our findings indicate that an existing mechanosensitive osteocytic repair program is suppressed by MM cells, which can be reinvigorated via a brief single loading session. It suggests that exercise-based interventions may be beneficial to restore bone mass through endochondral ossification programs in patients with MM.

affiliations: Department of Chemical Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China.

Computational strategies provide complementary tools for analyzing and optimizing RNA sequence, structure, function, and delivery, accelerating the rational design of RNAs and the optimization of delivery systems. This review systematically introduces two core advances in the field of RNA therapy: (1) the design and optimization of RNAs based on predictive modeling and algorithmic screening; (2) the intelligent transformation of the delivery system through data-driven methods. This review not only summarizes computational approaches developed to address key challenges in RNA therapeutics, but also highlights opportunities for integrated RNA-delivery co-design. These advances may provide useful insights for the development of next-generation precision therapeutics and their future clinical translation.

affiliations: Division of Endoscopy Hirosaki University Hospital Aomori Japan.
records.abstract: Endoscopic stricturotomy (ES) is a novel approach for treating benign strictures of the lower gastrointestinal tract. However, it is performed at a limited number of facilities, and strategies for preventing complications have not yet been established. We performed ES for ileo-sigmoid anastomosis associated with Crohn's disease (CD). Although endoscopic dilatation was successful, delayed bleeding occurred. Endoscopic hemostasis provided temporary relief, but delayed bleeding recurred nine times within 17 days after ES. Combined hemostatic treatments with vascular forceps soft coagulation, biocompatible synthetic peptide gel, and endoscopic clips failed to stop recurrent bleeding. Infliximab infusion was also unsuccessful. Finally, wound coverage with polyglycolic acid (PGA) sheets prevented rebleeding and avoided abdominal surgery. Here, we report that covering with a PGA sheet and fibrin glue may be useful in preventing recurrent delayed bleeding after ES for anastomosis associated with CD.

affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology Toyohashi Municipal Hospital Aichi Japan.
records.abstract: Ménétrier disease (MD) was diagnosed based on hypoalbuminemia and giant gastric folds extending from the body to the fundus in a woman in her 70s. A serum anti- Helicobacter pylori antibody test and urea breath test yielded negative results. Remission was achieved with steroid therapy, and she was relapse-free with the use of a proton pump inhibitor. Annual esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) was continued for gastric cancer surveillance. Fifteen years after the diagnosis of MD, a type 0-I well-differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma was detected on the posterior wall of the upper gastric body. EGD, computed tomography, and endoscopic ultrasonography revealed no findings suggestive of MD recurrence, and the lesion was considered intramucosal. Endoscopic submucosal dissection resulted in curative en bloc resection. Histopathology revealed no evidence of active MD. The patient remained free of MD relapse and gastric cancer recurrence. MD is characterized by giant gastric folds and protein-losing gastroenteropathy, and it is considered a risk factor for gastric cancer. However, reports of gastric cancer diagnosed at an early stage and treated endoscopically during long-term follow-up after clinical remission induced by medical therapy, as in the present case, are rare. This case highlights the importance of continued endoscopic surveillance for gastric carcinogenesis even after long-term clinical remission of MD.

records.title: Preoperative Diagnosis of the Bile Duct Traumatic Neuroma by Endoscopic Ultrasound-guided Tissue Acquisition: A Case Report.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology Shiga University of Medical Science Hospital Shiga Japan.
records.abstract: Traumatic neuroma of the cystic duct stump is a rare benign lesion that may mimic biliary malignancy, making preoperative diagnosis challenging. We report a case of an enhancing lesion at the cystic duct stump after cholecystectomy that was diagnosed by endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition (EUS-TA). Imaging studies revealed an 8-mm enhancing nodule at the cystic duct stump, and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography showed a unilateral filling defect at the corresponding site. Peroral cholangioscopy demonstrated smooth mucosa without irregular vessels, suggesting a submucosal lesion rather than mucosal malignancy. EUS revealed a well-demarcated, homogeneous hypoechoic mass immediately distal to the origin of the remnant cystic duct. EUS-TA using a 22-gauge needle enabled TA from the lesion. Histopathological examination showed proliferation of spindle-shaped cells with wavy nuclei, and immunohistochemical staining was positive for S-100 protein, confirming the diagnosis of traumatic neuroma. No procedure-related adverse events occurred, and unnecessary surgical resection was avoided. EUS-TA may facilitate preoperative diagnosis of cystic duct stump traumatic neuroma and help guide appropriate management.

Early symptoms are often subtle, leading to late-stage diagnosis in the majority of patients and a missed window for optimal treatment. Therefore, more sensitive diagnostic approaches are urgently required to improve survival rates and reduce the disease burden. Compared with traditional imaging and tissue biopsy, novel biosensors have become important tools for lung cancer diagnosis due to their high sensitivity, non-invasiveness and rapid detection abilities. Aptamers, a class of single-stranded DNA/RNA molecules capable of specific target recognition, are ideal for the development of efficient lung cancer biosensors owing to their low synthesis cost, high stability, minimal immunogenicity, and ease of modification. This review focuses on the application of aptamers in lung cancer detection, summarizes current developments in aptamer-based sensors (aptasensors), and critically compares the analytical performance, clinical limitations and translational obstacles of five mainstream aptasensor platforms, then discusses their challenges and future perspectives, aiming to promote more accurate and efficient early-diagnostic techniques for lung cancer.

records.abstract: Primary esophageal extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) is extremely rare, and its optimal management has not been established. We report a case of primary esophageal MALT lymphoma that was successfully treated by endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). A 70-year-old woman presented with an elevated lesion in the lower esophagus that was detected incidentally on computed tomography. Endoscopy and endoscopic ultrasonography revealed a subepithelial lesion confined to the submucosal layer without apparent invasion of the muscularis propria. Although an endoscopic biopsy suggested a low-grade lymphoma, a definitive diagnosis could not be established because of the limited tissue volume. Therefore, ESD was performed to obtain an adequate specimen for definitive diagnosis, and complete resection was achieved as a result. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examinations of the resected specimen confirmed primary esophageal MALT lymphoma. The patient has remained in complete remission for 3 years without additional therapy. This case suggests that ESD may be a diagnostic and therapeutic option for primary esophageal MALT lymphoma. Trial Registration : N/A.

records.title: Ulcerative Esophagitis With Marked Eosinophilic Infiltration and Fluorodeoxyglucose-Positron Emission Tomography Positivity Requiring Differentiation From Esophagogastric Junction Carcinoma.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterological Surgery Nippon Medical School Hospital Tokyo Japan.
records.abstract: Esophagitis with marked eosinophilic infiltration, including eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), can rarely present with ulceration or stricture. We report a rare case of positron emission tomography-positive esophagitis with marked eosinophilic infiltration accompanied by ulceration and stricture, requiring differentiation from esophagogastric junction carcinoma. A 50-year-old man with no history of allergies underwent computed tomography, which revealed para-esophageal lymphadenopathy and circumferential thickening of the distal esophagus. Endoscopy showed an ulcerated stricture with an iodine-unstained area. Positron emission tomography demonstrated fluorodeoxyglucose uptake at the lesion site. Multiple endoscopic biopsies (11 specimens) were negative for malignancy but revealed 70 eosinophils per high-power field, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for EoE. Hiatal hernia was also observed, suggesting the possibility of concomitant reflux esophagitis. Significant dysphagia persisted due to the severe stricture. Therefore, endoscopic bougie dilation was carefully performed under general anesthesia. After 8 weeks of proton pump inhibitor therapy, mucosal healing was confirmed, and topical steroids were initiated for persistent eosinophilic infiltration. This case highlights that esophagitis with marked eosinophilic infiltration accompanied by ulceration and stricture may require differentiation from cancer.

records.title: Gastric Metastasis of Uterine Leiomyosarcoma Detected During Surveillance Endoscopy and Resected by Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection After Multiple Metachronous Metastases: A Case Report.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterological and Pediatric Surgery Faculty of Medicine Oita University Japan.
records.abstract: Uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) is a rare, aggressive uterine malignancy that usually metastasizes hematogenously, whereas gastrointestinal involvement is uncommon. A 69-year-old woman with uLMS treated by hysterectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy developed metachronous lung, sigmoid colon, gallbladder, and abdominal wall metastases. After treatment of these metastases, periodical surveillance endoscopy revealed a 15-mm subepithelial lesion with a shallow central depression in the lower gastric body. Endoscopic ultrasonography showed a well-defined submucosal lesion without muscularis propria invasion, and biopsy confirmed metastatic leiomyosarcoma. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) was performed, achieving en bloc resection without adverse events. This rare metachronous combination of gastric, colonic, and gallbladder metastases highlights that incidental gastric metastasis may occur during prolonged disease courses and suggests that ESD may be a useful minimally invasive option for local control of small gastric metastases.

affiliations: Cancer Biology Program, Karmanos Cancer Institute, Wayne State University School of Medicine, Detroit, MI 48201, USA.

Originally identified as TRAIL-inducing compound 10 (TIC10), ONC201 is a first-in-class small molecule distinguished by a unique pharmacologic profile. It promotes apoptosis through multiple convergent mechanisms, including upregulation of TRAIL, activation of the integrated stress response (ISR), direct allosteric activation of the mitochondrial protease ClpP, and antagonism of dopamine receptor D2 (DRD2). These pathways converge to engage both extrinsic and intrinsic apoptotic programs, disrupt mitochondrial bioenergetics, and reprogram survival signaling, distinguishing ONC201 from conventional cytotoxic and targeted agents. Preclinical studies have demonstrated broad antitumor efficacy across diverse cancer models. Clinically, ONC201 has progressed rapidly through early-phase trials, establishing a favorable safety and pharmacokinetic profile, with sustained biological activity and weekly oral dosing. Pivotal trials in H3 K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma demonstrated meaningful clinical benefit, leading to accelerated regulatory approval and making it the first therapy to receive such approval for this devastating disease. Ongoing studies are expanding ONC201's clinical applications to hematologic malignancies and gynecologic cancers, as well as to combination regimens. records.title: Gut microbial histamine and serotonin promote cerebrovascular angiogenesis: Evidence from moyamoya disease.
affiliations: Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Diagnosis and Treatment of Major Neurological Diseases, Guangzhou, Guangdong 510080, China.
records.abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by arterial stenosis and compensatory neovascularization, but its upstream drivers remain poorly defined. Here, we identify Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum ( B. pseudocatenulatum ), a traditionally probiotic species, as a context-dependent pathobiont. Integrated metagenomic and metabolomic analyses revealed enrichment of B. pseudocatenulatum in MMD, closely associated with elevated microbial-derived histamine and serotonin. In mice, chronic oral administration of B. pseudocatenulatum disrupted intestinal barrier integrity and increased gut microbial production and systemic levels of histamine and serotonin. These changes were accompanied by systemic inflammation and activation of angiogenic pathways, which together promoted MMD-relevant cerebrovascular remodeling in experimental models. Notably, direct administration of histamine or serotonin to mice reproduced key MMD-like vascular phenotypes, supporting the conclusion that these microbial metabolites are sufficient to induce selected MMD-relevant vascular changes in experimental models. Our findings propose a microbial-metabolite-vascular axis and suggest that the role of specific Bifidobacterium strains may be more nuanced than previously recognized. records.title: <i>Fusobacterium nucleatum</i>-mediated tryptophan metabolic reprogramming facilitates immunosuppression and metastasis in triple-negative breast cancer.
affiliations: Key Laboratory of Clinical Laboratory Diagnostics (Ministry of Education), College of Laboratory Medicine, Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing 400016, China.
records.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum ( F. nucleatum ) is a prevalent Gram-negative anaerobic bacterium commonly found in the oral cavity. Recent studies have shown that F. nucleatum colonizes breast cancer by binding to Gal-GalNAc through the adhesin Fap2, but how they regulate the tumor microenvironment remains unknown. Here we observed an enrichment of F. nucleatum in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) relative to ER + and HER2 + breast cancer subtypes, and found that F. nucleatum promoted lung metastasis and immunosuppression in TNBC. Mechanistically, F. nucleatum promotes tryptophan metabolism in TNBC by up-regulating the tryptophan metabolic enzyme IL4I1 through the IL20-JAK-STAT4 signaling axis, thus inhibiting the effect of anti-PD-1 antibody immunotherapy and promoting lung metastasis and immunosuppression. Collectively, our findings shed light on the process by which F. nucleatum promotes lung metastasis and immunosuppression in TNBC, and provide evidence for finding new therapeutic targets and strategies for TNBC.

records.title: Charting the landscape of microbiota in bladder cancer: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
affiliations: Department of Urology, Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan 410008, China.
records.abstract: The microbiota refers to the assemblage of microorganisms present in a particular environment, which can maintain homeostasis and modulate immune function in the human body. Microbiota dysbiosis disrupts bodily functions, leading to a series of human diseases, including cancer. Recent studies have suggested that tumor microbiota play important roles in the tumorigenesis of bladder cancer (BLCA), including malignant proliferation, invasion and metastasis, chemo-radiotherapy resistance, and immune response. In this review, we systemically classify the microbiota of the digestive and urinary systems associated with BLCA, as well as the intratumoral microbiota within BLCA tissue. This review provides a comprehensive summary of the characteristics of these microbial populations and explores their potential roles in the development, detection, diagnosis, and treatment of BLCA, with a focus on immunotherapy, while also discussing existing problems and possible development directions. Given the complexity and breadth of this field, clinicians should carefully consider the influence of the microbiota throughout the entire diagnostic and therapeutic process for BLCA.

records.abstract: This study developed and validated a non-invasive multi-metabolite magnetic resonance spectroscopy framework for preoperative molecular subtyping of adult diffuse gliomas. Using a cross-center, cross-vendor cohort of 268 patients, 48 features derived from 18 metabolites were systematically evaluated to identify discriminative metabolic signatures for predicting IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion status. The integrated metabolic model showed robust intra-center and cross-center performance for IDH prediction, with AUCs of 0.906 and 0.857, respectively, and for 1p/19q prediction, with AUCs of 0.858 and 0.787, respectively. These results suggest that synergistic metabolic profiling support molecular assessment in patients who may not be suitable for invasive biopsy.

records.title: Mapping intestinal microenvironment heterogeneity in Hirschsprung's disease by spatial transcriptomics: Role of THBS1 in macrophage polarization and neural stem cell regulation.
affiliations: Department of General Surgery and Trauma, National Clinical Research Center for Child Health and Disorders, Ministry of Education Key Laboratory of Child Development and Disorders, Chongqing Key Laboratory of Structural Birth Defect and Reconstruction, Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing 400014, China.
records.abstract: The pathogenic role of the intestinal microenvironment on Hirschsprung's disease (HSCR) is increasingly recognized; however, the spatial expression patterns and underlying molecular mechanisms of the HSCR intestinal microenvironment remain unclear. In this study, we generated the first comprehensive spatial transcriptomic map of HSCR and revealed microenvironmental heterogeneity. Spatial transcriptomics revealed THBS1 as a consistently down-regulated gene in HSCR aganglionic segments. In vitro experiments using THP-1 and SH-SY5Y cells showed that THBS1 promoted M2-like polarization and interacted with SDC1. Furthermore, THBS1-overexpressing macrophages enhanced the proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells in co-culture. These findings suggest a potential role for THBS1 in modulating macrophage-neural interactions in the HSCR microenvironment, though further validation in primary cells is needed.

records.title: Case Report of a Rapidly Progressive Indolent T-Cell Lymphoma of the Gastrointestinal Tract.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology Institute of Science Tokyo Tokyo Japan.
records.abstract: Indolent T-cell lymphoma of the gastrointestinal tract (iTCL-GI) is a relatively newly recognized disease entity. iTCL-GI was first proposed by Perry et al. in 2013, before it was formally incorporated as a distinct disease category in the fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Hematolymphoid Tumors: Lymphoid Neoplasms in 2022. Although the prognosis of iTCL-GI is generally favorable, some cases may present with malignant transformation or severe clinical manifestations. Herein, we describe a case of iTCL-GI with a poor clinical outcome. An 85-year-old female presented with chronic diarrhea and weight loss. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy and colonoscopy performed at the referring clinic were nondiagnostic, and the patient was referred to our institution. Balloon-assisted enteroscopy revealed multiple ulcerative lesions in the distal ileum, which were eventually diagnosed as iTCL-GI based on the biopsy findings. Palliative care was provided in accordance with the patient's preferences. Her gastrointestinal symptoms progressed rapidly, and she died 5 months after symptom onset. In this report, we discuss how balloon-assisted enteroscopy can be useful in the diagnosis of iTCL-GI, as well as a review of the literature on potential risk factors for poor clinical outcomes, including the presence of ulcers on endoscopy.

records.abstract: Objectives Underwater endoscopic mucosal resection (UEMR) is an established treatment for non-pedunculated colorectal lesions, but securing an adequate resection margin can be difficult in selected cases due to poor visualization or snare instability. This retrospective study evaluated the technical outcomes and safety of this step-up strategy for non-pedunculated lesions measuring 10-20 mm. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 56 consecutive 10-20 mm non-pedunculated colorectal lesions treated with UEMR as the first-line approach between September 2024 and September 2025. When predefined intra-procedural criteria for UEMR difficulty were met, the procedure was converted to UIEMR. The primary endpoints were technical success (en bloc and R0 resection rates) and procedure-related adverse events of the step-up strategy. Results Resection was completed using UEMR alone in 31 lesions, whereas 25 lesions required conversion to UIEMR. En bloc resection was achieved in all lesions, and histologically negative margins were reported in all cases. No delayed bleeding or perforation was observed. Conclusion For 10-20 mm non-pedunculated colorectal lesions, a step-up strategy with UEMR first and selective conversion to UIEMR was feasible and safe and may be a practical treatment option.Clinical trial registration: N/A.

records.title: Localized Gastrointestinal Light Chain (AL) Amyloidosis Under Surveillance for Five Years: A Case Report.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology Dokkyo Medical University School of Medicine Tochigi Japan.
records.abstract: Amyloidosis, characterized by the deposition of abnormal protein fibrils in organs, is classified as systemic or localized. Amyloid light chain (AL)-type localized amyloidosis is uncommon, particularly when confined to the gastrointestinal tract. Herein, we report a case of localized gastrointestinal AL-type amyloidosis that was incidentally detected and remained endoscopically and clinically stable over a 5-year follow-up period. The patient, a man in his 40s, had undergone a colonoscopy for colorectal cancer screening, during which scattered erosions were detected in the colon. Amyloid deposits were identified on biopsy. No cardiac or renal involvement, or evidence of multiple myeloma, was found. He was ultimately diagnosed with localized AL-type gastrointestinal amyloidosis. Following diagnosis, the patient underwent regular surveillance with transoral and transanal small-bowel endoscopy. No endoscopic progression or gastrointestinal symptoms were observed during the follow-up period, and the patient remained asymptomatic. This case suggests that conservative observation may be reasonable in carefully selected patients after exclusion of systemic involvement.

records.title: Efficiency and Safety of Endoscopic Injection Sclerotherapy With Ligation for Esophageal Varices: A Retrospective Study.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology Yamagata University Faculty of Medicine Yamagata Japan.
records.abstract: Objectives Endoscopic injection sclerotherapy with ligation (EISL) is a combined endoscopic treatment that involves endoscopic injection sclerotherapy (EIS) and endoscopic variceal ligation. This study aimed to compare the efficacy of conventional EIS and EISL in treating esophageal varices and the usefulness of EISL. Methods A total of 104 cases treated with conventional EIS and 44 cases treated with EISL for esophageal varices were included in the study. The procedure duration, intra-injection volume, and para-injection volume, the success rate of intravascular injection based on variceal type, recurrence-free survival, and post-treatment adverse events were assessed. Results The procedure duration was significantly shorter in the EISL group (13.1 ± 7.2 min) than in the conventional EIS group (20.7 ± 8.0 min; p p = 0.0426). The intravascular injection success rate was higher in the EISL group for all variceal morphologies, particularly for F1/F2 esophageal varices. In terms of post-treatment adverse events, the frequency of fever was lower in the EISL group than in the conventional EIS group ( p = 0.008). There was no significant difference in recurrence-free survival between the conventional EIS and EISL groups. Conclusions Compared with conventional EIS, EISL required shorter procedure times and reduced paravariceal leakage of the injected sclerosant. EISL also demonstrated higher success rates, particularly for small varices, and fewer post-treatment adverse events.

records.title: Phase I/II Prospective Study on Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Hepaticogastrostomy as Primary Drainage for Unresectable Malignant Hilar Biliary Obstruction.
affiliations: Department of Gastroenterology Aichi Cancer Center Nagoya Japan.
records.abstract: Objectives Various drainage methods have been used for unresectable malignant hilar biliary obstruction (MHBO). However, controlling cholangitis and obstructive jaundice is still challenging. We performed a phase I/II study of endoscopic ultrasound-guided hepaticogastrostomy (EUS-HGS) as primary drainage for MHBO. Methods This prospective Phase I/II study included 20 patients requiring biliary drainage for MHBO recruited from June 2021 to December 2023. The primary endpoint was safety. The secondary endpoints were clinical efficacy, reintervention methods, and frequency. Results The types of bile duct stenosis were Bismuth type I/II/IIIa/IIIb/IV; 4/1/5/3/7 cases. Fifteen cases (75%) had cholangitis before the EUS-HGS was performed. Technical success rate; 100% (20/20), clinical success rate; 75% (15/20). The four cases in which clinical success was not achieved were Bismuth type IV with cholangitis and obstructive jaundice, and all cases required additional drainage for the right bile duct.Early adverse events were stent migration: one case (severe) and peritonitis: one case (mild). Conclusions The safety of EUS-HGS for the primary drainage of unresectable MHBO is acceptable. Regarding clinical efficacy, based on the results observed in patients with Bismuth type IV obstruction, we acknowledge that further investigation is warranted. records.title: Desmoid Fibromatosis of the Gastric Wall Mimicking Needle Tract Seeding after Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Fine-Needle Biopsy for Pancreatic Cancer: A Case Report.
affiliations: Department of Internal Medicine Division of Gastroenterology Asahikawa Medical University Hokkaido Japan.
records.abstract: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) is widely used for the pathological diagnosis of pancreatic diseases. However, needle tract seeding (NTS) remains a clinical concern, particularly when the puncture route is not included in the surgical resection field. We report a case in which distinguishing NTS from other pathologies was challenging. A woman in her 70s underwent EUS-FNB via the gastric antrum for a 10-mm pancreatic head lesion, which was diagnosed as adenocarcinoma (cT1bN0M0, Stage IA). She subsequently underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy (pT3N0M0, Stage IIA) without adjuvant chemotherapy. Two years postoperatively, a 30-mm submucosal tumor was detected in the stomach. Although positron emission tomography-computed tomography demonstrated fluorodeoxyglucose uptake, three separate sessions of EUS-FNB failed to yield a definitive diagnosis, with NTS being strongly suspected. Partial gastrectomy was performed. Histopathology revealed a fascicular proliferation of spindle-shaped cells with nuclear β-catenin positivity, leading to the diagnosis of a desmoid fibromatosis (DF). This case underscores that although NTS should be considered when a lesion arises along the EUS-FNB puncture tract, alternative diagnoses, including DF, must also be carefully evaluated.

records.abstract: Bladder cancer (BC) is an aggressive and treatment-resistant malignancy with a high recurrence rate. Current first-line therapies only provide limited relief due to chemoresistance and toxicity. Natural products are emerging as promising chemotherapeutic agents due to their multi-target mechanisms and excellent safety profile. In this study, we evaluated the anti-BC effects of echinocystic acid (EA), a pentacyclic triterpenoid, on BC cells and investigated the underlying mechanism. We found that EA effectively inhibited proliferation, triggered G1-phase cell cycle arrest, and simultaneously suppressed cellular invasion and migration capabilities in vitro . Although EA did not obviously induce apoptosis in BC cells at the doses that were effective in suppressing their growth, it successfully triggered ferroptosis within these cells. Moreover, EA suppressed xenograft tumor growth of BC cells in vivo and demonstrated a favorable safety profile. Mechanistically, EA interacted with AKT1, reducing its phosphorylation and thereby inhibiting the AKT1/GSK3β/β-Catenin signaling pathway. Furthermore, EA exhibited synergistic effects with gemcitabine in inhibiting BC cells in vitro and in vivo . Overall, our results suggest that EA may exert its anti-BC effects, at least in part, by inhibiting the AKT1/GSK3β/β-Catenin signaling pathway. affiliations: Department of Hematology, Shandong Provincial Hospital Affiliated to Shandong First Medical University, Jinan, Shandong 250021, China.
records.abstract: Lipid metabolism reprogramming is the key mechanism for tumor cells to meet the material and energy required for rapid proliferation. This process involves the comprehensive remodeling of fatty acids, cholesterol, and phospholipid metabolic networks, and drives malignant transformation and disease progression by synergistically regulating the core links of lipid synthesis, uptake, transport, oxidation, and storage. Among them, the reprogramming of fatty acid metabolism plays a key carcinogenic driving role, and its abnormal regulation runs through the whole process of tumor development. Hematological malignancies are characterized by rapid proliferation and high metabolic demands, and rely on the lipid-rich bone marrow microenvironment. For this reason, tumor cells establish unique metabolic adaptability by reconstructing the key metabolic pathways of fatty acids to resist stress such as hypoxia and nutritional deficiency. This metabolic reorganization not only enhances the proliferation and survival advantages but also enhances stemness, promotes chemotherapy resistance, and disrupts signaling pathways, thus constituting a critical basis for disease progression. Targeting the dysregulated fatty acid metabolism has become a highly promising treatment direction, providing new possibilities for the precise risk stratification and improvement of therapeutic effect in different subtypes of hematological malignancies. records.title: A panoramic study of circulating tumor DNA in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
affiliations: Department of Hematology, China-Japan Union Hospital of Jilin University, Changchun, Jilin 130033, China.
records.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a frequently encountered aggressive form of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, characterized by significant clinical and molecular heterogeneity. Owing to inherent limitations of traditional treatments for DLBCL, the advent of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) detection, coupled with the integration of multi-omics technologies, has brought about substantial advancements in the diagnosis and treatment of this disease. This review elaborates on the evolution of ctDNA detection and multi-omics integration, its applications in early diagnosis, prognostic model construction, and treatment decision-making, as well as drug resistance mechanisms, highlighting that ctDNA is a powerful tool but faces technical, biological, and clinical implementation barriers that need to be overcome for wider clinical use.
